picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt
picks.blurb: Pitt hasn't allowed a point in the first or third quarter this season. Pitt also hasn't left Pittsburgh. That changes today at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, when the Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) walk into a sold-out Lane Stadium to face a Virginia Tech team (4-0, 1-0 ACC) chasing its first 5-0 start since 2005. The winner moves into a three-way tie for first place in the ACC. "It'll be one of the louder games we play," Pitt head coach Pat Narduzzi said this week. Here are three bold predictions for the game. 1. Jeffrey Overton Jr. runs for 100 yards on the nation's No. 4 run defense Pitt has allowed 213 rushing yards in four games. Overton ran for 209 yards last Saturday at Boston College, including the 76-yard touchdown that put Virginia Tech ahead for good in a 21-14 win. That earned him ACC Running Back of the Week. The sophomore missed the first eight games of last season with an injury and finished 2025 with 25 carries. He already has 60 this fall, for 409 yards and four rushing touchdowns at 6.8 yards per carry. He'll run Friday without left tackle Justin Terry, who is out. That's a real problem against a defense allowing 53.3 rushing yards per game. 2. Mason Heintschel leaves Blacksburg without a touchdown pass Pitt's sophomore quarterback has thrown 13 touchdown passes, second in the ACC. Seven came against Miami (Ohio). Six came against Bucknell. Against UCF and Syracuse, he went 28 of 52 for 335 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. The Panthers got past Syracuse by running for 245 yards, and true freshman running back Damon Ferguson Jr. leads the team with 239 yards for the season. Virginia Tech has to take that away first. Then comes the hard part for Heintschel. This is his first road start of the season, against a defense that leads the nation with 45 tackles for loss and 17 sacks. The risk sits behind Virginia Tech's front. Maryland threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns on the Hokies two weeks ago, and Virginia Tech has one interception in four games. Defensive coordinator Brent Pry's group doesn't have to be perfect. It has to make Heintschel uncomfortable, and no defense in the country has lived in the backfield more. 3. John Love hits a walk-off field goal, and Virginia Tech is ranked by Sunday John Love has scored 313 points in a Virginia Tech uniform. The next three decide Friday night. "This is going to be a battle," Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin said Monday. Franklin would know. He faced Narduzzi four times from 2016-19 when he was at Penn State. Pitt leads the ACC at 8.5 points allowed per game and hasn't given up more than 14 to anyone. I have Virginia Tech get past that number, but not by much. The Panthers stay in it on the ground, the way they did against Syracuse. That leaves it to Love. The fifth-year kicker is fourth on Virginia Tech's all-time scoring list, has a career-long of 60 yards, and went 2 for 2 at Boston College. He gets one more with the clock running out. Virginia Tech wins 24-21. The Hokies have 86 points in the AP poll, fifth among teams outside the Top 25, and haven't been ranked since 2021. With a win on Friday night, it will be hard to leave them out for another week. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. Virginia Tech is favored by -3.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -172. The total is set at 54.5 points. Here's my Pitt vs. Virginia Tech prediction and college football pick for Friday, October 2, 2026. Pitt vs. Virginia Tech Pick: Virginia Tech ML -172 (Play to -195) My Virginia Tech vs. Pitt best bet is on the Hokies to win the game outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Pitt vs Virginia Tech Odds Pitt vs Virginia Tech point spread : Virginia Tech -3.5 (-106), Pitt +3.5 (-114) Pitt vs Virginia Tech over/under : 54.5 (-118o / -104u) Pitt vs Virginia Tech moneyline : Pitt +142, Virginia Tech -172 A season ago, Pittsburgh went 7-1 against teams outside the final top 40 in SP+, winning by an average margin of 41.3-20.3. Against teams inside the final top 40, Pitt went 1-4 and was outscored 32-21.6. To begin 2026, Pitt is 2-0 against non-power conference teams, winning by an average score of 59-7; it's 2-0 against power-conference teams, winning by an average score of 19.5-10. Granted, the Panthers' 12-7 win over UCF was riddled with rain delays and general field slop (and rain impacted its game against Syracuse ), it's pretty clear Pitt continues to tear through lesser opponents and play markedly different against teams more equal in talent. The rest of the schedule is against an ACC slate, meaning we'll get a pretty good idea of who Pitt is by Halloween. Injuries have also been to blame for sporadic offensive shortcomings. QB Mason Heintschel continues to shine. His 1,191 yards passing ranks third in the ACC and his 10 graded big-time throws lead the league, but he's had to operate without top running back Ja'Kyrian Turner (left Week 1 and hasn't played since) and Malik Knight (missed the last two games). Starting safety Cruce Brookins also missed last game. In Turner's absence, freshman Damon Ferguson Jr. has stepped into the lead back role, rushing for 102 yards against Syracuse. Under Pat Narduzzi, you know what you're getting with Pittsburgh: a tough football team that rolls right over lesser competition but gets outplayed and out-coached by the big boys on the schedule. On Friday night, Pitt gets its first "big boy" in Virginia Tech. Box score watchers might be quick to jump to Virginia Tech 's 21-14 win over hapless Boston College and point fingers at James Franklin. Keep in mind, that game was played in the middle of a nor'easter with wind gusts clocking in at over 40 miles per hour and driving rain soaking Alumni Stadium. Nobody could keep their footing. It was like toggling on Even Teams when playing EA College Football 27. Many of the issues that plagued Franklin's Penn State teams have shown up early in the season. The fact of the matter is, Ethan Grunkemeyer isn't a very good passer on the aggregate, though he's able to make infrequent spectacular plays. The Hokies are perfectly fine chunking their way down the field and trying to control the pace defensively to suffocate the opponent. It's absolutely worked so far. But unlike Franklin at Penn State, Virginia Tech has allowed its opponents to cover their tracks late in games. This season, Virginia Tech led Maryland 35-14 (final: 35-26) and Old Dominion 44-13 (final: 44-21). In State College, Franklin was notorious for covering spreads late if able to. The Hokies field both an offense and defense inside the top 30 nationally in points per drive and thrive with a strong defensive front and exceptional secondary, even if neither unit has really been tested yet this year. As a favorite, Franklin touts a 73-52-3 ATS record (58.4%) during his career, including a 3-1 mark this season (the one ATS loss coming last week). Until 2025, the year it all fell apart at Penn State, Franklin hadn't lost as a favorite since 2021 (-4 favorite at No. 12 Michigan State ). Both teams' offenses look spectacular against outmatched opponents and not as great in driving rain (who would have guessed?). Both have benefitted from strong defensive line play, minimal turnovers or penalties and a pretty favorable schedule all around. Both coaches are veterans and both quarterbacks are flawed. There's a pretty even playing field here. But Franklin is the more trustworthy coach despite a slipping public perception … for some reason. At Penn State, his problem was not getting over the biggest contenders in the country, not losing to lesser opponents (Matt Campbell, looking at you). This is a situation where, at Penn State, Franklin has an excellent track record. Here at home, that track record continues. Virginia Tech has the coaching edge, the home-field edge and a roster comparable, if not superior, to Pitt's (and healthier). The Hokies take this Friday night game at home in front of what should be a classic juiced Lane Stadium crowd. Pick: Virginia Tech ML -172 (Play to -195)

Virginia Tech Athleticse Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - Virginia Tech football takes on Pitt tomorrow night in its fifth contest of the 2026 season. Ahead of the Friday evening clash against the Panthers, three members of our staff offered their thoughts on what could unfold tomorrow: JACKSON CAUDELL: This is the biggest Virginia Tech game in years. If they win, they will be 5-0 and have a win against one of the teams expected to compete for a spot in the ACC Championship game, giving them a huge tiebreaker. You could argue that the winner of this game is going to be in the best position to make it to Charlotte and likely face Miami . I expect this to be a close game, but the home-field advantage and Virginia Tech's defense are going to be the difference. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 20 JAMES DUNCAN: Nobody has scored on Pitt in the first or third quarter this season. The Panthers allow 8.5 points per game, fewest in the ACC. Against a Virginia Tech line missing left tackle Justin Terry, I don't see the Hokies hanging 40. Expect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer to live on quick throws to tight end Luke Reynolds. But Pitt has been flagged 37 times for 359 yards, all at home. Now its first road trip is Lane Stadium on a Friday night. If pre-snap penalties have been an issue at home, who knows what it will be in front of 65,000 people screaming at the top of their lungs when trying to hear a snap count. I still expect this game to come down to the final snap. In fact, I'm predicting a walk-off field goal from John Love to give James Franklin his signature moment in his first season at Virginia Tech. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 21 THOMAS HUGHES: Virginia Tech has an opportunity to turn a promising start into a true renaissance Friday night. Pitt presents a challenge on defense, and the Hokies will need to help Ethan Grunkemeyer avoid spending the evening under pressure. Quick throws to Luke Reynolds and a productive rushing attack should be central to that effort, and they should be more available than in last Saturday's rainy affair in Chestnut Hill. Still, I trust Virginia Tech to find enough offense to keep this game within reach throughout. The bigger question is whether the Hokies can force Pitt into the mistakes that become increasingly costly in a close conference matchup. Lane Stadium should have something to say about that, particularly if the Panthers struggle with penalties. I expect a competitive game that remains undecided into the fourth quarter, but that Virginia Tech's defense delivers the final stop to keep James Franklin's team unbeaten and firmly in the ACC conversation. picks.headline: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt
picks.blurb: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CBS parts ways with analyst Tony Romo TRENDING Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Virginia Tech Athletics Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - For the first time in 20 days, Virginia Tech football hosts a game at Lane Stadium - this one against Pitt with a 5-0 start hanging in the balance. Both the Hokies (4-0, 1-0 ACC) and Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) enter Friday night's contest with unblemished marks, making the matchup one of four games nationally this week between undefeated FBS teams. For Virginia Tech, a victory would secure its first 5-0 start since 2005 and continue a remarkable turnaround in James Franklin's first season at the helm. Virginia Tech's perfect record hasn't come without adversity. After opening the season with commanding victories over VMI (73-3) and Old Dominion (44-21), the Hokies survived consecutive road tests against Maryland and Boston College . Tech defeated the Terrapins 35-26 before escaping a rain-soaked Chestnut Hill with a 21-14 victory. The latter required Virginia Tech to overcome a 14-6 fourth-quarter deficit. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 14-yard score to Marlion Jackson, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. broke free for a 76-yard touchdown less than three minutes later to put the Hokies ahead for good. Overton's emergence has added another dimension to an offense that relied heavily on Grunkemeyer through the first three weeks. The sophomore enters Friday with 409 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 60 carries, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt. He erupted for a career-high 209 yards on 25 carries against Boston College, earning ACC Running Back of the Week honors. Finding similar success against Pitt, though, will be difficult. The Panthers enter Blacksburg allowing just 53.3 rushing yards per game and 8.5 points per contest. Pitt's defense has surrendered just 34 points through four games, following a 59-14 win over Miami (Ohio) with victories of 12-7 over UCF, 27-13 over Syracuse and 59-0 over Bucknell. That creates perhaps the game's most important matchup. Virginia Tech has found a potential difference-maker in Overton, but Pitt possesses one of the stingiest rushing defenses in the country. If the Panthers can prevent Overton from consistently reaching the second level, more responsibility will fall back onto Grunkemeyer. The Penn State transfer has largely handled that responsibility well. Grunkemeyer has completed 101 of 136 passes for 1,012 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Boston College limited him to 147 passing yards, but the weather played a significant factor. Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel has completed 88 of 130 passes for 1,191 yards, 13 touchdowns and just one interception. His season began with a historic seven-touchdown performance against Miami (Ohio), and he threw for 403 yards and six touchdowns in last week's demolition of Bucknell. Heintschel became the first ACC quarterback to record multiple six-touchdown passing games in the same season. That should provide Virginia Tech's pass rush with its biggest challenge yet. The Hokies have consistently disrupted opposing backfields, entering Friday averaging 4.25 sacks and 11.3 tackles for loss per game. Cortez Harris has led that charge with five sacks, including two in the victory over Boston College. Getting to Heintschel could be critical. Pitt averages 347.3 passing yards and 39.3 points per game, and its passing attack isn't dependent on a single target. Thirteen different Panthers caught a pass against Bucknell, while five players hauled in touchdowns. Censere Lee led the scoring barrage with three touchdown receptions. Friday also represents something Pitt hasn't experienced this season: a road game. The Panthers played each of their first four contests at Acrisure Stadium and now head into a sold-out Lane Stadium for a primetime matchup. Pitt is 3-8 all-time in Blacksburg, although the Panthers have won three of the last four overall meetings between the programs. Virginia Tech won the most recent matchup, 38-21, in 2023. Virginia Tech has answered four different tests through four weeks. Pitt presents another, and perhaps the most complete one yet. One undefeated record will disappear Friday night. Which one do I think will? Virginia Tech's defense should give Pitt its toughest test yet, while Lane Stadium could make the Panthers' first road game uncomfortable. The Hokies may not completely contain Heintschel, but Overton and Grunkemeyer should generate enough offense late to preserve the unbeaten start in a tightly contested ACC matchup. away.headline: Two new players land on Pitt injury report vs. Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Defensive end Zach Crothers and tight end Elijah Lagg have both been listed as doubtful to play against the Hokies. Receiver Tony Kinsler has been upgraded to probable after being tabbed as questionable on Wednesday. Safety Cruce Brookins is still questionable to suit up. Two new players have popped up on the availability report for Pitt on Thursday night ahead of Friday night’s clash with Virginia Tech in Blacksburg. Panthers head coach Pat Narduzzi isn’t thrilled that his team has to deal with another short week before an ACC matchup, after previously beating Syracuse on a Thursday earlier this season. “I wish we didn’t have two short weeks (for) two ACC games,” Narduzzi said on Wednesday in his office at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. “When you talk about conference play, it’s most important, and our first two games are short weeks and different weeks. I think it certainly helps us (having played) on a Thursday night. Although the schedule’s totally different, I think it does help us play in a mid-week game.” Both teams enter the primetime matchup at 4-0, but neither are ranked. There is also an undercurrent with James Franklin and Narduzzi having been painted as adversaries since the former’s time at Penn State.

away.headline: Week 5 Practice Update – Hokies prepare for their biggest test yet against Pittsburgh
James Franklin gives mixed results in terms of injury news ahead of the Pitt showdown
away.blurb: The week before the BC game, the Hokies lost Justin Terry to an injury against Maryland, and he missed the game in Chestnut Hill and was replaced by Oklahoma transfer Logan Howland. Unfortunately, on Monday, Franklin said that Terry is going to be out for several weeks with his injury, per Andy Bitter of Tech Sideline . James Franklin gives mixed results in terms of injury news ahead of the Pitt showdown Skip to main content About Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball A third of the way through the 2026 season, injuries are building for the Virginia Tech football team along the offensive line. First-year head coach James Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore have had to move people around and make adjustments on the fly. That was the case leading into last weekend's battle at Boston College. There was a lot of moving around, and Montavious Cunningham missed the game after suffering an injury last week, but at his weekly press conference on Monday, Franklin sounded like someone who was fairly confident that he might be getting some injured players back against Pittsburgh on Friday night. James Franklin gives injury updates ahead of Pitt showdown However, there was slightly better news when it came to Cunningham. The Georgia State transfer missed the game, but Franklin is expecting to have him back when the Panthers visit on Friday night. If that is the case, then it would be a big development against a stout Pitt defensive line. Another key player who missed the Boston College game was wide receiver Ayden Greene. Marlion Jackson filled in for him and hauled in a big fourth-quarter touchdown pass from quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer that tied the game after Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s two-point conversion run. Greene is one of the top receivers for offensive coordinator Ty Howle, and Franklin is also anticipating him to be back on Friday night, per Bitter . Now, there are still four days until the kickoff time against Pitt approaches, and things can certainly change. However, it would be a big lift if the Hokies could get back either Cunningham or Greene, or even both of them, in a battle between two undefeated teams. Loading recommendations... home.headline: Virginia Tech football's initial injury report brings both good and bad news
home.blurb: On Tuesday, the initial availability report for the Pitt game was released. Greene and Cunningham were listed as probable, while Terry was listed as out, something that wasn't a surprise after Franklin's comments on Monday . According to David Cunningham of Tech Sideline , Brody Meadows and Cunningham were participants in practice on Tuesday, but did not go through the one-on-ones against the defense. That is a sign that, despite being listed as probable, Cunningham might not go this week against the Panthers either. It's a short week for the Virginia Tech football team after they rallied in the fourth quarter for a 21-14 win last Saturday afternoon at Boston College. Trailing 14-6, the Hokies scored on back-to-back drives late for their first ACC win under James Franklin. The short week means everything moves up a day, including gameday to Friday night, when Virginia Tech hosts Pittsburgh in a battle of two 4-0 teams at Lane Stadium . Franklin and his staff are dealing with some injuries a third of the way through the season, and the initial availability report for Friday night's game was released, and it brought some promising news for the Hokies. Initial availability report brings mixed news for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Last week, the Hokies were thin on offense. The week before, against Maryland, offensive lineman Justin Terry went down with an injury in the second quarter; wide receiver Ayden Greene did, too. Then, before the Hokies flew to Boston, offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham popped up on the injury report. That would be a big loss of a veteran lineman ahead of one of the biggest games in Blacksburg in years. That would force Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore to shuffle more for the game, and likely during it as well. That's less than ideal. As far as Greene goes, it sounds promising that he could play against Pitt, and that would be big for quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer and offensive coordinator Ty Howle. If not, Marlion Jackson should get more reps after he played against BC and hauled in a fourth-quarter touchdown reception that eventually led to a tie game after Jeffrey Overton Jr. added the two-point conversion. There are still a couple more days before kickoff, and the true test will be pregame warmups on Friday night. picks.blurb: Penn State vs. Northwestern Predictions: Week 5 Stress Test for Nittany Lions Skip to main content SI.COM OLYMPIC SPORTS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS A year ago, James Franklin walked off the Beaver Stadium field for the last time after Penn State's 22-21 loss to Northwestern. The Wildcats turned a fourth-quarter drive into the game-winning touchdown that ended Franklin's tenure as Penn State's head coach. On Friday night, the Nittany Lions get another crack at the Wildcats, this time as part of a grand opening. Northwestern will host Penn State in the first game at the new Ryan Field, a nearly $900 million venue that claims to be the most expensive college stadium ever built. There are plenty of Penn State storylines Friday night beyond a mostly new program getting proxy retribution for last year's loss at Beaver Stadium. More than half of Penn State's roster wasn't on the field that night and doesn't care about settling scores. These Nittany Lions want to settle their offense. With that in mind, here's how we see Friday's Penn State-Northwestern game shaking out, including our predictions from the Penn State on SI staff. Kickoff is scheduled for just after 8 p..m. ET on FOX. 1. Penn State vs. Northwestern game predictions Penn State Nittany Lions quarterback Rocco Becht (3) gestures at the line of scrimmage against the Wisconsin Badgers at Beaver Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Fisher: A movable object (Penn State’s inconsistent rush offense) meets a stoppable force (Northwestern’s second-worst Big Ten rush defense) Friday. If the Nittany Lions’ rushing attack finally shows signs of life, it’s going to be hard for the Wildcats defense, which allows 417.3 yards per game, to get stops. Penn State bounces back in a big way and silences a likely raucous Northwestern crowd. The Nittany Lions’ defense will likely keep them close, but there’s too many questions for the offense to expect a win. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. ET on FOX. Penn State is favored by -2.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -140. Northwestern, meanwhile, enters as a +2.5 underdog and is +116 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 45.5 points. Here's my Penn State vs. Northwestern prediction and college football pick for Friday, October 2. Penn State vs. Northwestern Pick: Over 45.5 My Northwestern vs. Penn State best bet is on both teams to go over the total. Penn State vs Northwestern Odds Penn State vs Northwestern Spread : Penn State -2.5 (-115), Northwestern +2.5 (-105) Penn State vs Northwestern Over/Under : 45.5 (-108o / -112u) Penn State vs Northwestern Moneyline : Penn State -140, Northwestern +116 Head coach Matt Campbell had one of the easiest schedules for the Nittany Lions heading into Week 4. A devastating loss to Wisconsin saw a 17-7 halftime lead evaporate after producing just a field goal in the second half. The Badgers dominated in overall yards per play, outgaining the Nittany Lions by nearly two yards per play. The loss of star wide receiver Koby Howard left quarterback Rocco Becht without answers in the passing game. Penn State generated a low 23% Success Rate on 31 passing attempts, completing just one pass over 20 yards. Defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn has produced one of the best units in FBS against the pass, producing the top overall coverage grade, per PFF . The Nittany Lions held the Badgers to just 36% of available yards and a 30% Success Rate on passing downs, both under the national average. Limiting methodical drives has been the calling card for the defense, although teams with explosiveness on the ground have created issues for the Nittany Lions. Penn State has allowed five different rushing gains over 50 yards this season. A surprising cover against Indiana could be linked to execution in the passing game. Quarterback Aidan Chiles continues to learn Chip Kelly's offensive requirements, connecting on 22-of-29 passing attempts for two touchdowns. Northwestern converted half of its third- and fourth-down attempts with an average distance to go of 9.9 yards against the Hoosiers. Slot receiver Luke Dehnicke doubled his season target share as a home-run hitter in the passing game, while Chiles' safety blanket in the red zone came in the form of wideout Griffin Wilde . Head coach David Braun has plenty of work to do regarding the defense. The Wildcats rank dead last in producing a pass rush and sit bottom-10 in Line Yards. Northwestern elects to play quarters zone coverage, giving up the middle of the field and opting to make stops in scoring position. Opponents have marched up and down the field, but Northwestern ranks 17th in Defensive Finishing Drives thanks to 19 opponent drives crossing the 40-yard line with an average of 2.4 points per trip. The Wildcats have allowed the third-fewest red-zone touchdowns with four on the season. The star of the game might not be either team, but rather the grand opening of Ryan Field in Chicago. There are significant changes in the elements of Northwestern home games, as the playing surface has been lowered to 21 feet below ground level. Many media tours of the stadium noted that with wind gusts at 20 MPH in Evanston, but the wind wasn't a factor from field level. Similar to Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, the roof and open outer perimeter allow the wrinkles of gusts to smooth out before hitting the field. From an investment perspective, totals should be treated differently for Northwestern home games with a slight upward trajectory in scoring. The biggest question comes in Northwestern's ability to create explosive rushes against Penn State's defense. The Wildcats have notched only one rush that exceeded 30 yards this season, signaling that Chiles' mobility in the passing game will be the plan of attack. Lynn's defense lines up in Cover 3 and Cover 1 zone, both of which Chiles has dominated this season. Northwestern has a 56% Success Rate on 90 offensive snaps against those coverages, averaging a big play on 21% of attempts. Penn State will counter with a successful rushing attack behind James Peoples , Carson Hansen and Quinton Martin Jr. Campbell's offense has logged more than 80 rushing attempts using inside and outside zone read, a run concept Northwestern has severely struggled to defend. The Wildcats own a low 41% Success Rate against zone read, a number that drops to 35% against Campbell's base personnel of 12. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings call for Penn State to be favored by a field goal, aligning with the current market offering. A projected total of 48.5 shows there's a small advantage against a sinking number of 45. Penn State will have an advantage on the ground with 12 personnel and zone read, while Chiles and Northwestern will look to expose a Nittany Lions defense that has given up numerous explosive runs. Look for both teams to create methodical drives and enough scoring opportunities. Pick: Over 45.5

The Nittany Lions will visit Northwestern on Friday evening as the Wildcats proudly open the doors to the newly renovated Ryan Field for the first time. That figures to make for a bit of a challenge as Northwestern will be fired up to show off their new digs and pick up a big win in conference play after an incredible effort last week on the road against Indiana. On the other hand, Penn State is merely looking to rebound after a tough loss at home last week to Wisconsin that saw the Nittany Lions blow a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter. The optimism for Penn State on the road against Northwestern may have dipped in the span of the past week, for good and understandable reasons, but the staff at Nittany Lions Wire still seems to think Penn State will find a way to come out of the week with a win. Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 5 game against Northwestern, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer We saw last week that Penn State's offense really missed the likes of rising star wide receiver Koby Howard. This week, there can be no excuse for not having something going in the passing game. I think that means Rocco Becht needs to get into a comfort zone with his tight ends a bit more instead of looking for some big plays down the field from the receivers. So for the second week in a row, I'm looking for Ben BRahmer to be a difference maker for the offense. If Penn State can get that, then they should be in good enough shape to get out of Evanston with a hard-fought win. Northwestern will not make anything easy on the Nittany Lions. This may need to be a bit of a scrappy win from the offense. Final score prediction: Penn State 20, Northwestern 18 Player of the game pick: Ben Brahmer, Penn State tight end Paul White, Contributor This Northwestern team just took Indiana down to the wire, so I'd imagine a Penn State win would have to be in a close game. That doesn't sound like such a fun idea after last week's game, but hopefully we can keep our composure this time Final score prediction: Penn State 27, Northwestern 24 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor The Nittany Lions find themselves in a similar position to last year as they face Northwestern after an inexplicable loss yet again. This time, it's on the road as Northwestern opens up the new Ryan Field. In order to spoil affairs, the Nittany Lions have to get going in the passing game and take advantage of what could be an aggressive Wildcat defense. Look for Chase Sowell to step up in the continued absence of Koby Howard and be the difference in a game that could come down to the last few plays. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . picks.blurb: Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus CBS parts ways with analyst Tony Romo TRENDING Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup (Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Penn State Nittany Lions will be looking to get back on track tomorrow against Northwestern , in what could be a tough game for the team. Penn State fell 24-20 to Wisconsin last week in what was one of the more surprising scores from the weekend. But the Nittany Lions believe that the loss to the Badgers was more of an outlier, and this team still has a lot to play for this year. As the team gets ready for the Wildcats, the Nittany Lions will need to make sure that they don't overlook them. Northwestern has played much better to start the season than they have in year's past, opening the year 2-1 under head coach David Braun. For Penn State, this can be a bounce-back game, with the team getting things right after the tough loss against Wisconsin. But Friday night games can be tough, especially having to go on the road. Heading into the game, the Nittany Lions are favored to win the contest, but not by too much. According to ESPN , Penn State is being given a 55.9 percent chance to take down Northwestern on the road. If the Nittany Lions are going to win this game, everything starts and end with quarterback Rocco Becht . Becht has looked good to open the year, throwing for 865 yards with nine touchdowns and one interception. But against the Badgers, Becht struggled, throwing for just 114 yards and one interception. The veteran signal-caller will need to get back on track in this game against Northwestern if the Nittany Lions are to have a shot at winning. Coming over from Iowa State with head coach Matt Campbell, Becht gives Penn State a legitimate option under center. But he has bene prone to some inconsistency at times during his career, and last week was one of those moments for him. Northwestern has its own star quarterback in Aidan Chiles , who transferred to the team this offseason. So far, Chiles has played very well for the Wildcats, throwing for 807 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions. If Penn State can find a way to slow him down, it could make life much easier to grab the win. But Chiles has turned this offense around, and this will be something that the Nittany Lions will need to focus on throughout the game. Overall, Penn State needs to take down Northwestern if they want a chance to make the College Football Playoff this year. The Nittany Lions are off to a good a start this year, even with the loss last week, and this game offers them a chance to turn the page.

The Nittany Lions allowed a 17-point comeback in the 24-20 home loss. This week is a new week. Penn State must defeat Northwestern in Evanston to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. A loss almost certainly kills any chance of making the postseason tournament. The players held a meeting on Monday to make sure that "everyone's on he same page" after the loss. Friday will determine the impact of that meeting. Game: Penn State Nittany Lions (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten) @ Northwestern Wildcats (2-1, 0-1 Big Ten) History: 16-6, Penn State Last Meeting: 22-21, Northwestern (2025) Time: Friday, 8 p.m. (EST) Location: Ryan Field | Evanston, Ill. Radio: 99.5 FM | 103.7 FM | 1450 AM | SiriusXM 84, 257, XM App Odds: Penn State -2.5 | O/U: 45.5 Penn State vs. Northwestern Preview Injuries, Preview & Prediction This will be the 23rd meeting between Penn State and Northwestern. The Wildcats took a 22-21 win over the Nittany Lions in Beaver Stadium last season in what was James Franklin's final game at Penn State. The Nittany Lions are 7-3 all-time at Ryan Field, but Friday night will be the opening of the brand-new Ryan Field, an $870 million 35,000-seat stadium. Daryus Dixson Listed as Questionable Starting cornerback Daryus Dixson was listed as questionable on the initial and Wednesday availability reports. Dixson has started all four games and has allowed only three catches for 28 yards in coverage. Matt Campbell said Wednesday that Dixson was "dinged up" before halftime last week against Wisconsin, but he did practice on Wednesday. Not much has changed besides Dixson's status. Penn State is still waiting for Koby Howard and LaVar Arrington II to return from their injuries. Backup kicker Cristiano Rosa is a new addition to the availability report and is listed as out. Scouting the Wildcats On the other side of the availability report, Northwestern's starting tight end Luke Dehnicke has been downgraded from questionable to doubtful. He is the Wildcats' second-leading receiver with 11 catches for 208 yards. Northwestern also has starting corner Braden Turner and starting safety Damon Walters listed as questionable. Starting corner Josh Fussell is listed as doubtful. Northwestern took No. 5 Indiana to the brink on the road last Friday night. The Hoosiers escaped with a 29-23 victory. Wildcats transfer quarterback Aidan Chiles had perhaps his best game of the young season, passing for 293 yards and scoring three total touchdowns. His favorite target, however, was Dehnicke, who had seven catches for 140 yards. Northwestern's leading receiver, Griffin Wilde , had both receiving touchdowns. That's a big hit to Northwestern's passing attack if Dehnicke can't go. Last week against Wisconsin, Penn State struggled to cover Badgers tight end Jacob Harris , who had five catches for 105 yards, including the 72-yard score to seal the game. Dehnicke has played roughly half of his snaps from the slot this season and would likely be matched against one of Penn State's safeties, Jeremiah Cooper or Marcus Neal Jr. Neal really has struggled this year. He allowed both of Wisconsin's fourth-quarter touchdowns and has given up the most receptions and yards of anybody in Penn State's secondary. Northwestern has not done well establishing the run this year. The Wildcats rank 95th in the nation in rushing yards per game, and had only 32 yards and a touchdown by Chiles against Indiana. Photo Courtesy: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images On defense, the numbers are less impressive for Northwestern. The Wildcats' run defense has struggled, ranking 128th in the nation. The Hoosiers rushed for 271 yards and two touchdowns without leading rusher Turbo Richard for most of last week's game. Backup Lee Beebe Jr. had 24 carries for 203 yards and a score. Northwestern's pass defense isn't stellar either, ranking 80th in the country. This could be a big game for Penn State's receivers Brett Eskildsen , Chase Sowell and Zay Robinson . Sowell was the only wideout to record a catch in last week's loss. Eskildsen was able to break loose deep a few times, but Rocco Becht was off his game most of the night and missed multiple throws. While Northwestern's passing attack is very solid, it'll be difficult to throw against Penn State's No. 4-ranked pass defense, especially if Dixson is healthy. Running likely won't be much easier, but Penn State has struggled to contain scrambling quarterbacks like Chiles so far. This also could be a breakout game for Penn State's run game , and the same for the passing attack if the Wildcats are down three starting defensive backs. If Penn State's offense can get back on track against a weaker defense than Wisconsin's, then the first game at new Ryan Field will likely go to the visitors. away.headline: Penn State week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
away.blurb: It’s still early in the year, but the injury bug has already bitten Penn State hard, forcing star wide receiver Koby Howard to miss the start of conference play. Howard’s absence was significant in the Nittany Lions Week 4 loss to Wisconsin, and he’ll be out again on Friday night when Matt Campbell’s team helps open the newly rebuilt Ryan Field at Northwestern. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. Dixson was on the initial injury report on Tuesday night, listed as “questionable,” and held the same status on Thursday night when the availability report was released about 24 hours before kickoff in Evanston. The return of Alex Tatsch, who missed Week 1 as he ramped up from an injury he suffered preparing for the Pinstripe Bowl in December, has helped to fill the void left by Smith and Kooper Ebel, and Tony Rojas has been rock-solid at the second level of D’Anton Lynn’s defense. Dixson is seemingly the only player on Penn State’s roster whose status is uncertain heading into Friday night. Considering he played through the injury in the second half against Wisconsin, his outlook appears favorable, but that he wasn’t upgraded to “probable” raises a legitimate question about whether or not he’ll be ready to suit up against the Wildcats. Notable Northwestern injuries: Luke Dehnicke still doubtful While not ruled out, Northwestern has two starters listed as doubtful for Friday night, including its second-leading receiver: tight end Luke Dehnicke. Dehnicke caught seven passes for 140 yards against Indiana in Week 4, but was banged up and could miss Week 5. The Wildcats may also be without starting defensive back Braden Turner. Fellow starting DB Damon Walters is listed as questionable. Here’s a look at the full report: This article was originally published on victorybellrings.com as Penn State Week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up . Howard, however, isn’t the only injury situation the Nittany Lions are dealing with. There’s another member of the 2025 recruiting class who has turned into a key cog for Penn State, whose situation is worth monitoring: cornerback Daryus Dixson. Penn State needs to get back into the win column after melting down in the second half last week, and Campbell is still in search of his first Big Ten win. To get it, the Nittany Lions will need to be at full strength. Here’s a look at the injury report: Cam Smith is the notable downgrade from the early-week report. Sophomore cornerback Daryus Dixson apparently struggled with an injury during the Wisconsin game and is currently listed as questionable for the game against Northwestern . For Dixson, this could be a minor setback for what has been looking like a breakout season for the young corner. He recorded his first interception of the season last week and played the most snaps out of anyone on the defensive side of the ball. Most impressively, he has only allowed three receptions all season long, with the longest only being 16 yards. Against Buffalo, he also recorded a blocked field goal, proving his versatility and importance to the squad. While Dixson should be good to go should he miss the Northwestern game, others are not as lucky. Defensive end Max Granville suffered a season-ending injury in the first game of the season, his second in as many years. As for Koby Howard , no one knows when he will likely return, but to expect him to only miss a couple of games would be wishful thinking. Penn State fans can only hope this Dixson injury is the last of its kind this season. The Crimson Tide moved to 4-0 with a devastatingly dominant 49-18 win against South Carolina . Sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell was flawless with 365 yards passing and four touchdowns. Mississippi State is in the midst of one of the great starts in program history, reaching consecutive 4-0 starts for the first time since World War II. The Bulldogs came from behind to stun No. 19 Missouri 31-24 behind 360 yards and three touchdowns from superstar quarterback Kamario Taylor . Alabama has dominated the matchup between these two teams all-time, holding an 86-18-3 advantage, including a 40-17 win in 2023. However, the last MSU win came in Nick Saban's first season -- can the Bulldogs turn the Tide? Alabama vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Super Kamario: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor has been the story of the early college football season. The Macon, Mississippi, native dreamed of playing in Starkville, and leads the SEC with 344.3 yards of offense per game. Taylor has thrown for at least three touchdowns in every start, including in road trips to Minnesota and South Carolina. With him in the lineup, suddenly anything seems possible at Mississippi State. Russell's rise: Taylor might be the best quarterback in the nation; he also might not be the best quarterback in this game. Since throwing a pair of interceptions in his first SEC start against Kentucky , Russell has been astonishing, throwing for 685 yards and seven touchdowns on 77% completion in wins over Florida State and South Carolina. Behind Russell's explosion, Alabama leads the nation in points per game against Power Four competition at 48.0 points per game. Best on worst: With so much attention on the quarterbacks, the secondaries will take center stage. Mississippi State has the worst passing defense in the SEC statistically, but the Bulldogs rank ahead of the Tide in both yards per attempt and passer rating allowed. Mississippi State has recorded nine sacks in four games, but getting a consistent pass rush could change the game. picks.blurb: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS STATE SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS STARKVILLE — It's been nearly two decades since Mississippi State felt the joy of a win against Alabama. Sylvester Croom was roaming the sidelines as first-year coach Nick Saban and his Crimson Tide program were in the midst of a late season slide. Fast-forward 20 years and its Kalen DeBoer leading the way, looking to lead his team to 5-0 record for the first time in his tenure. On the flip side, Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby is looking to earn the first signature win of his young head coaching career while hosting No. 7 ranked Alabama for a nationally televised showdown on ABC. Here's everything you need to know to be prepared for what's a pivotal weekend for the Bulldogs program. Mississippi State Bulldogs running back Fluff Bothwell (24) and wide receiver Zion Ragins (7) react after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Game Information Game Information Mississippi State vs. Alabama Crimson Tide When : Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026 Kickoff Time : 11 a.m. CT Venue : Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, Mississippi TV Channel : ABC Radio : Bulldogs Sports Network Series Record : Alabama leads 86-18-3 Betting : Alabama (-5.5), O/u: 60.5 total points ( FanDuel ) DISCLAIMER : Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. What ESPN Thinks The brand of Alabama remains strong on the national radar and that's no different this week at ESPN with the Crimson Tide given a 74.2% chance of going into one of the most hostile atmospheres in all of college football and pulling out a win, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Mississippi State State continues its climb up the FPI rating system, coming in this week at No. 9 among SEC teams and No. 20 overall with key victories on the road at Minnesota and South Carolina plus another against then No. 19 Missouri. This starts one of the stiffest stretches for any team as the Bulldogs are set for a murderer's row-level slate with Alabama coming Saturday, proceeded by a BYE, on the road at LSU, home against Oklahoma and then another road trip to Austin to face the Texas Longhorns. The Bulldogs chances of winning out are slim at 0.1%, but do have a 97.5% chance of at least reaching bowl eligibility with six wins. When it comes to making the playoffs, Lebby's team has the sixth-best odds SEC teams at 23.8% to at least make the field, 1.6% to make the championship game and 0.5% chance to win the national championship. ESPN FPI (SEC) Rankings 1. Georgia 2. Texas 3. Alabama 4. LSU 5. Florida 6. Tennessee 7. Texas A&M 8. Ole Miss 9. Mississippi State 10. Oklahoma 11. Auburn 12. South Carolina 13. Missouri 14. Kentucky 15. Vanderbilt 16. Arkansas Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer walks off the field after a victory against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What DeBoer Is Saying What DeBoer Is Saying One of the hardest things for a coach to prepare his team for in a road game at Davis-Wade Stadium is the cadence of cowbells. Thousands of cowbells. "Personally, this is one of those stadiums that I haven't played in no matter where I've been," DeBoer said Monday. "What I hear from the people that I trust, is that it's going to be an absolutely crazy environment. We're going to be prepared for that. We talked about as a team this morning and we're looking forward to that challenge. "We know, this week, we've got to work on that crowd noise. There will probably be a lot of cowbells that we're hearing in practice in one form or fashion. Another thing is that it's just an early game. It's an 11 o'clock kickoff. We're a morning practice team and we've had some success in those morning games. We've got to go on the road and travel that morning. It's going to be a little different set-up that way too." The Bulldogs' defense has been very active this season at stopping explosive plays and keeping everything in front of them. They're disciplined, bring elite energy and effort with each down. "They play complementary football. They get the ball back, get off the field and get the ball back to the offense. I think it's timely stops. It's a group effort of guys flying around. They're going to be multiple in what they show you. "I have a lot of respect for them and what they are doing this time of the year. I think complementary football is what they're doing really well at Mississippi State. They're explosive. Obviously, that defense has to face that offense every day in practice. It's high level across the board." Mississippi State Bulldogs head coach Jeff Lebby looks on during the second quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Lebby Is Saying What Lebby Is Saying The Crimson Tide offense is full of big play athletes at nearly every position. Whether that's done with Keelon Russell's dual-threat combination, a four-headed backfield, Ryan Williams or any other weapon, Lebby knows his defense has to play assignment-driven, technically sound football to avoid allowing the game to get away from them early. "We're gonna have to do a great job tackling," Lebby said. "That's gonna be a huge piece of it. He's played really well. He's been incredibly productive. There's been explosive plays. He's got great talent around him. And so for us it's going to be about applying pressure, getting our fans really involved and excited about what's going on in between those white lines. "So for us it's kinda like I mentioned. We gotta get him off the spot and we've got to do a great job taking air out of it on the back end and making the plays when we get the chance." Alabama is tied for No. 24 nationally in sacks with 11 on the season. On the otherhand, Mississippi State has given up nine sacks on the season, which ranks No. 9 nationally, but the most alarming number was the four given up against Missouri in last week's 31-24 victory. And Lebby knows the biggest key to the Bulldogs upset bid will be keeping star quarterback Kamario Taylor upright to further establish himself as a Heisman Trophy contender. “[We] had moments where we were really clean, and had moments where we’ve got to continue to clean up,” Lebby said. “The fundamental pieces of it I’m gonna continue to talk about. Those guys playing clean fundamentally gives us the best chance to protect 1, but there were issues from a game standpoint. "We didn’t do a great job on the penetrator a couple times, and that’s part of being able to clean that up as we watch the tape, a huge focus for us this week.” Prediction : Mississippi State 42, Alabama 38 Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Former UCLA Coach Rick Neuheisel Predicts Winner of Alabama-Mississippi State Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS No. 7 Alabama (4-0, 2-0) travels to Davis Wade Stadium to face No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0, 2-0) in the SEC's lone ranked matchup of Week 5 (Noon EDT, ABC). These two programs are separated by an hour and a half's driving distance and are meeting for the first time in three seasons. Alabama and Mississippi State have been traditional staples on each other's schedules, although the 86-18-3 advantage held by the Crimson Tide makes for the most lopsided series in SEC history. The Bulldogs' last victory was in 2007, Nick Saban's first season in Tuscaloosa. The closest Mississippi State came within the last 16 meetings was in 2017; the game was tied in the final 30 seconds, and Jalen Hurts hit then-freshman wide receiver DeVonta Smith for a 26-yard touchdown pass to win it 31-24. The matchup features a pair of high-octane offenses Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) throws the ball during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Keelon Russell has been fantastic for Alabama, but the most impressive part of the offense is the run game. The Crimson Tide has been questionable in that department for the better part of three seasons, and it has very quickly found a combination of offensive linemen and running backs to correct the deficiency. On the other side, Kamario Taylor has lived up to the hype for Mississippi State. He guided the Bulldogs to a pair of road wins at Minnesota and South Carolina to bring excitement to a fan base desperate for optimism, and he delivered a 31-24 win over Missouri to a packed Davis Wade Stadium under the lights in Week 4. Neuheisel: "I see two matchups here that are really cool." CBS Sports' "Inside College Football" panel predicted the winner of the game between Alabama and Mississippi State on Tuesday. Former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel pointed to a pair of critical matchups between the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs while making his game pick. "Number one is the quarterbacks," Neuheisel said . "These two guys are both going to play on Sundays, both have just unique frames. They're 19 years old and they're just getting started." Despite the intrigue in the quarterback matchup, Neuheisel pointed to the other matchup as a deciding factor due to the current weather forecast for Saturday. "The second matchup is between the two defensive coordinators," Neuheisel said. "Both have been head coaches: Kane Wommack was at South Alabama, Zach Arnett was ironically right here at Mississippi State, these guys know how to play field position defense. It's supposed to rain a lot during the game, I think I've got to go, in that situation with Alabama." Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CBS parts ways with analyst Tony Romo TRENDING Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State (David Leong-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Thu, October 1, 2026 at 1:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide are coming off of a dominant Week 4 win over South Carolina, which represented their most complete performance all season. Now, Alabama is preparing for its most difficult test yet , as the Crimson Tide are heading on the road to battle the upstart Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday. Like Alabama, Mississippi State is 4-0, and the Bulldogs are also fresh off of a very impressive victory, having topped Missouri last weekend. Mississippi State boasts an explosive offense, and while its defense certainly isn't among the best, it has a pair of terrific cornerbacks in Kelley Jones and Jett Jefferson that could pose some problems for Keelon Russell and Co. So, are the Crimson Tide on upset alert heading into Week 5? ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score of the matchup using his SP+ metrics, and while he does have Alabama coming out on top, he thinks it will be a nail-biter, projecting a 32-27 win for the Tide in Starkville. A victory would absolutely comprise Alabama's most impressive of the campaign to date and would set Kalen DeBoer's squad up very nicely as it continues to proceed into the most challenging part of its schedule, which begins with the clash against the Bulldogs. While the Crimson Tide are undefeated, things haven't necessarily been easy for them thus far. Alabama took care of business without breaking a sweat against East Carolina in its season opener, but it trailed Kentucky 17-13 at halftime in Week 2 before dominating the second half. It also fell behind Florida State 21-6 in the first half the following week, but ultimately rallied for a 50-36 victory. The Crimson Tide definitely avoided a slow start versus South Carolina last Saturday, taking a 35-3 lead at one point in a 49-18 triumph. One thing is for sure: the version of Alabama that showed up in Weeks 2 and 3 absolutely cannot expect to waltz into Mississippi State and emerge with a victory. The Bulldogs are a significantly better team than either Kentucky or South Carolina, and the Crimson Tide fall behind early, they could be in some serious trouble. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is one of the top Heisman Trophy candidates at the moment, and the Bulldogs also possess a terrific backfield led by Fluff Bothwell. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has also been a fast riser, too. Alabama cannot mess around this weekend.

Right tackle Jayvin James is questionable after leaving Alabama 's home win against South Carolina. Minnesota has won the Little Brown Jug just four times since 1968, while Michigan has taken it home on 44 different occasions (Michigan has covered in nine of the last 12 matchups). And though the Wolverines are coming off a tough loss to Iowa, I like them to cover -5.5 or better because of their defense. Nevertheless, oddsmakers still view the Wolverines as a solid favorite. They have history on their side, too. The Wolverines have dominated the Little Brown Jug rivalry, winning 27 of the past 29 meetings and not losing in Minneapolis since 1977. Can they continue that success and bounce back in a big way? Here are score predictions from MLive's beat writers: What a bizarre start to the season. Michigan finds itself 3-1 but this feels like a second "bounce back" game. With a bye looming, the Wolverines desperately need a win in Minneapolis. The good news? Michigan is coming off a largely well-played game … the defense pitched a shutout through three quarters while the offense showed serious strides moving the football. I expect more of the same on Saturday against a Golden Gophers team that wants to be balanced and play it safe. I'm not expecting all will be cured, but I do expect Michigan to have more firepower and enough explosive plays to come away with a win. Michigan 24, Minnesota 17 After letting what looked like a sure win against Iowa slip away last week, expect the Wolverines to play a more complete game against a Minnesota team they hold a clear talent advantage over. The Gophers' front seven is legitimate, led by preseason Defensive Player of the Year Anthony Smith, so generating consistent production on the ground may not come easy. Still, I think Bryce Underwood builds on last week's performance and continues to lean on his two favorite targets, Andrew Marsh and JJ Buchanan. Look for Michigan to bottle up Minnesota's rushing attack and force Drake Lindsey into a few costly mistakes through the air. The Wolverines win the game and the turnover battle, bringing the Little Brown Jug back to Ann Arbor. Michigan 27, Minnesota 17 Michigan's offense should continue its upward trajectory Saturday and find the end zone a few times. The defense might have a little more trouble than last week: Lindsey is efficient if not explosive and Minnesota has a stable of capable running backs. Michigan has questions along the offensive line but still has Bryce Underwood, Andrew Marsh, and JJ Buchanan. They've played in harsh environments — Michigan visited Oklahoma, Nebraska, and Michigan State last season, winning twice — and shouldn't be intimidated by (checks notes) Huntington Bank Stadium. Michigan's win streak at Minnesota is remarkable. It predates P.J. Fleck's existence. Continuing that streak won't be easy. I expect Saturday's game to come down to the final minutes. Will it be decided on the final play , as two of Michigan's games have already? I guess we'll find out. away.blurb: The players listed as OUT for Michigan are the same as Wednesday, and include offensive lineman Andrew Babalola, wide receiver Braydon Alford, running back Micah Ka'apana, running back Jonathan Brown, defensive end Julius Holly and offensive lineman Ace Hamilton. The players listed as QUESTIONABLE for the Wolverines are also the same, and include starting wide receiver Andrew Marsh, offensive tackle Andrew Sprague, starting edge Dom Nichols, starting edge John Henry Daley, reserve offensive lineman Houston Ka'aha'aina-Torres, and rhino lineman Manuel Beigel. Starting offensive lineman Blake Frazier was listed as PROBABLE for the second day in a row. On Monday, Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham was asked about the statuses of Daley and Blake Frazier. Frazier went down for several minutes in the second half, but did return to the game. Daley, meanwhile, went down with an apparent leg injury with two seconds to go in the game. The injury actually stopped the clock for Iowa, allowing the Hawkeyes to concoct their game-winning play in the 20-19 win as time expired. "Not definitive updates for their availability this week," Whittingham said. "It's still early in the week, obviously. So we'll just have to take it day-by-day at this point. We should have, by Wednesday would I think, a much clearer picture. I think that's the first day the Big Ten injury report comes out, so that'll coincide with when we have a pretty good handle on it." "We're on the way to clarity. We're closer to clarity than we were," Whittingham said. "We're not at a point where we know definitively one way or the other, but it's starting to come into focus a little bit. There's one or two more things that are going to be assessed or evaluated, and then we should have the clarity we need and whether he's going to become available. "If Blake's out, and Andrew is continuing to be out, and the Rhino's still out — we expect Manu (Beigel, who missed last week) to be back today. That's a positive, so hopefully we don't have that issue. "But if we lose another tackle, I guess there's some good news about Andrew Babalola. They're going to let him start practicing in one week, so apparently we'll get him back next week. We'll have to sit down and figure out the best combination, because that will put us in a little bit of a bind." "Nobody feels sorry for us, so we can't feel sorry for ourselves," Whittingham said. away.headline: Mounting injuries take a toll on Michigan offensive line
away.blurb: The Wolverines have started three different line combinations so far, and may have to go with a fourth this Saturday at Minnesota (12 p.m. ET, FOX) if tackle Blake Frazier — injured in the loss to Iowa — has to sit out. Those changes haven’t helped continuity, an important part of building a reliable offensive line, Harding admitted. Evan Link began the season at left guard, missed Week 2 due to injury and returned against UTEP as the starting left tackle, forcing Frazier to the right side to fill in for the sidelined Andrew Sprague. With Sprague’s status in limbo, and tackle Andrew Babalola ruled out since camp, Michigan has been shorthanded in recent weeks up front. When Frazier left the game last weekend against Iowa, a true freshman, Marky Walbridge, had to replace him. The good news — if there is some — is that there may be some light at the end of the tunnel. Harding is hopeful that Frazier may be able to suit up and play this Saturday, while Babalola is expected to be cleared to return next week. If he is, Babalola would have a full two weeks to reintegrate — Michigan is on a bye next week — before making his debut. ANN ARBOR, Mich. — While injuries and reshuffling have slowed the Michigan offensive line through four games, coach Jim Harding isn’t making excuses. The veteran o-line coach has seen it all and knows that a successful offense depends on the group up front, which he classified as a work in progress on Wednesday. “Truthfully, it’s not where I want it to be and where I think it can be,” Harding told reporters. “And that falls on me ultimately. You could say, ‘well, you’ve had this many injuries’ or ‘this many missed games,’ and frankly nobody cares. There’s injuries all across the country. We’ve got to do a better job.” “I think our pass protection so far has been really good, especially comparing the same players to last year,” Harding said. “I think we can be more consistent in the run game, getting more push.” Harding did see some good things against Iowa, who Michigan ran for 153 yards against, but explosive runs have been few and far between. Through four games, Michigan is averaging just 4.03 yards per carry and is one of nine FBS teams with one run of 20-plus yards or fewer. “The line of scrimmage was moving this past week, so that’s progress,” Harding said. “But it’s nowhere near where it needs to be in my opinion, or it should be. As frustrated as maybe some people are, there’s not anyone more frustrated (than me).” And then there’s the mystery with Sprague, who was suddenly scratched from the starting lineup the Friday before the UTEP game. If and when he returns, the Michigan would be six deep and in a much better spot. away.headline: Michigan's initial injury report for Minnesota game is quite concerning
away.blurb: The Michigan football injury report against Minnesota , at least the first report that came out on Wednesday had some surprises and raises some concerns. The Gophers will be a challenge. Michigan could also be without some of its best players. We knew John Henry Daley was going to be questionable . However, Andrew Marsh, who went over 100 yards last week, suddenly popped up on the injury report as questionable, which is essentially 50/50 that he will play. Andrew Sprague is also questionable. He's been out the past two weeks. Blake Frazier did a great job moving over to the right side in his absence. Frazier was injured against Iowa too, but he's probable for the Minnesota game. That's the one piece of good news. It's actually good news that Henry Daley is questionable. After he had a season-ending injury back in November, it's good to see he still has a chance to play this week. Dominic Nichols is also listed as questionable, which was his status last week, too. The arrow is pointing up. Hopefully, one of his top targets, Marsh, will be available on Saturday against Minnesota. Michigan, 3-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Iowa last Saturday, has to go through one more week before a bye week and a chance to rest up. In the meantime, Michigan has a challenging road game against the Golden Gophers, who knocked off Washington 27-24 last week. Thoughts on Michigan football injury report The idea of losing Marsh this week is a little scary. We all saw how difficult it was for Iowa to take away Marsh and JJ Buchanan. It was basically impossible. If the defense focused on one receiver or the other, Michigan just went the other way. There are plenty of other talented pass catchers to turn to. The Big Ten showdown brings a moment of tension for Ohio State, which suffered a 55-24 loss during its last visit to Kinnick Stadium in 2017. With one loss already, the Buckeyes can ill-afford a stumble as they enter a month that also includes trips to No. 6 Indiana and No. 18 USC . For Iowa, this represents a breakthrough opportunity on the heels of a last-second win at Michigan in Week 4. That victory propelled Iowa to 4-0 for the first time since 2021, when the Hawkeyes rose all the way to No. 2 in the AP poll on their way to an appearance in the Big Ten Championship Game. Beating the Buckeyes would put Iowa on a similar trajectory and send its playoff chances skyrocketing. Ohio State won the last two meetings by 28 (2024) and 44 (2022), but there are signs that these Hawkeyes are better equipped to stage a competitive battle as these Big Ten stalwarts square off in Iowa City for the first time in nearly a decade. Ohio State vs. Iowa: Need to know Iowa's offensive punch: Iowa ranks No. 48 nationally in total offense entering this showdown, which is hardly remarkable on the surface. But after ranking 117th or worse in total offense for the past five seasons, it's a marked improvement. The Hawkeyes struggled to run the football against Michigan last week, but quarterback Hank Brown led a game-winning drive capped by a touchdown pass to Reece Vander Zee on the game's final play. Considering the hostility of Michigan Stadium and the quality of the opponent, it was the sort of clutch, late-game execution that would have been unfathomable for the Iowa offense at any point over the past several years. Ohio State's defensive questions: Ohio State ranks just 27th in total defense through four games, down from finishing the 2025 season at No. 1 in that metric. Considering seven players from last season's defense were selected in the 2026 NFL Draft , it's not shocking that the Buckeyes have dropped off a bit. But the slide came with a cost in a Week 2 loss at Texas , when Ohio State's defense couldn't get off the field over the final 20 minutes as the Longhorns rallied from a 23-3 deficit to win 24-23. Illinois racked up 462 yards and 25 first downs on Ohio State last week. Though the Buckeyes won 42-19, it wasn't a banner day for coordinator Matt Patricia's defense, which comes into this game with some questions to answer. Jeremiah Smith making history: Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is on a blistering pace with 33 receptions for 617 yards and seven touchdowns through four games. The junior star is one touchdown away from tying Chris Olave for most receiving touchdowns in program history and just five away from matching ex-Michigan star Braylon Edwards for most receiving touchdowns in Big Ten history at 39. Smith is on track to become the first player to ever lead the Big Ten in receiving yards three times. He's also likely to surpass K.J. Hill and Emeka Egbuka for most receptions in Ohio State history in the near future. However, the Hawkeyes aren't quite as stingy on defense as usual, which means slowing the Buckeyes down enough to keep the game within two touchdowns could be hard. Look for Iowa to make this a competitive game until Ohio State's superior skill talent (see: Jeremiah Smith) creates separation down the stretch. If the Iowa Hawkeyes want to knock off Ohio State, things are going to have to break their way, but they also have to do their part in managing this game perfectly. It isn't just hoping to get the right bounce of the ball or be on the receiving end of a tipped pass like last week against Michigan. It requires some serious focus and attention, which is an area Iowa is an expert in. Kamari Moulton rushes for 100 yards Iowa knows it has to mitigate how many possessions Ohio State gets this week to stick around in this game and to keep the defense fresh. The Hawkeyes are going to give a heavy dose of running the ball to ensure that's the case. Kamari Moulton should be fresh after just 13 carries against Michigan last week. Expect Tim Lester and the offense to ask a lot of Moulton in this one. It may not be a consistent barrage of five yards on each touch. It is likely to be a case of banging into a brick wall for two and three yards at a time before Kamari Moulton pops a few chunk plays. Jeremiah Smith is held under 100 receiving yards Jeremiah Smith has been held under 100 yards just once this year. It wasn't by a bad game. Against Kent State, he had five receptions for 85 yards in a 59-3 win. It was to keep him healthy. His other games? He has had games of 151 yards, 164 yards, and 217 yards. He is doing whatever he wants, whenever he wants, against defenses. Phil Parker has been around the block once or twice before, and he has tried to contain stars before. Iowa is likely to throw the kitchen sink at Smith with double coverage, or safety help at the least, to force other Buckeyes' wide receivers to step up. Iowa forces at least 2 turnovers The Hawkeyes' defense knows they have to steal possessions in this game and create short fields for the offense. That's not meant as an indictment of the offense. Instead, it's a compliment to Ohio State. The Buckeyes are explosive, and taking the ball away from them is going to be key for Iowa this week. I expect Iowa to be hyper-aggressive in punching at the ball to force a fumble this week on each run play. If Iowa can steal a short field and translate that into three or seven points, with the clock running, that's a gigantic win for the Hawkeyes. Loading recommendations... Happy prediction Friday, Hawkeye fans! Tomorrow is the day you've all been waiting for for some time - a colossal matchup at Kinnick Stadium between No. 14 Iowa and No. 5 Ohio State on Saturday (2:30 p.m. CT, CBS). After careful consideration, here's how I see this battle playing out. Where/When To Watch Matchup: No. 5 Ohio State (3-1, 1-0) @ No. 14 Iowa (4-0, 1-0) Scheduled game time: Oct. 3 at 2:30 p.m. CT Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Weather: 68 degrees Announcers: Brad Nessler (play-by-play), Charles Davis (analyst), Jenny Dell (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Cole Krueger) Before we talk about the actual football game, let's begin this pick by talking about the electric atmosphere we're about to witness inside Kinnick Stadium on Saturday. This is easily Iowa's biggest home game at least in five years (No. 3 Iowa vs. No. 4 Penn State in 2021), and you probably have to go all the way back to the 2006 showdown between the Hawkeyes and Buckeyes to find a more important game in Iowa City. Iowa fans have waited for this game since the schedule came out in February, and the buzz in this city is palpable right now. College GameDay returning for the first time in 20 years has only increased it. The crowd might be the only advantage Iowa has on the gridiron, though. Though it blew a 20-point fourth quarter lead at Texas a few weeks ago, Ohio State still might be the most-talented team in the nation. The Hawkeyes are going to have their hands full against the Buckeyes, but the one thing Iowa will always have? Heart. That competitive grit was evident in the thrilling comeback victory over Michigan last weekend, and the Hawkeyes will certainly need it to keep pace with an explosive Buckeye offense. Speaking of offense, how will Iowa stop Jeremiah Smith? Smith is not only the best wide receiver in the country, he may just be the best player in the entire sport. Not only is he fast and an excellent route runner, his 6-foot-4, 222-pound frame makes him a dangerous threat in 50/50, red zone situations. Smith is likely going to make a few big plays in this game, but what concerns me the most is Iowa trying to get pressure on Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin. The Hawkeyes are never going to be a blitz-first team under Phil Parker, but have you seen how accurate Sayin is? He's not much of a running threat, but Iowa has to get pressure on him if it wants to stay in this ballgame. I think the Hawkeyes will get to Sayin a few times, but I don't think it's going to be enough. Iowa is going to cover the spread and move the ball against a shaky Ohio State defensive front , but the Buckeyes just make a few more big plays to pull away for a victory. away.headline: Where Jay Timmons landed on Ohio State football’s first injury report vs. Iowa
away.blurb: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Jay Timmons’ status is uncertain for Ohio State football’s game at Iowa on Saturday. The freshman starting defensive back was listed as questionable on the first availability report of the week. The Buckeyes also listed right tackle Phillip Daniels and tight end Bennett Christian as questionable. No regular contributors were ruled out for the matchup. Defensive end Zion Grady, who hasn’t played since a Sept. 5 loss at Texas, was not on the report, meaning he’s available to play at Iowa. Daniels hasn’t played for Ohio State since he was injured late in a win at Texas. Christian hasn’t played since a Sept. 19 win against Kent State and was listed as out last week. Timmons has been Ohio State’s starting nickelback since the season started. He signed with the Buckeyes as a five-star prospect in the 2026 recruiting class, flipping his commitment from Florida State. In four games this season, Timmons has eight tackles and a forced fumble. He was injured in the second half of Saturday’s win against Illinois. The Buckeyes will release updated injury reports Thursday, Friday and Saturday. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC.
