picks.headline: Greg McElroy Picks Florida-Missouri Winner in High-Stakes Week 5 SEC Showdown
picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks Florida-Missouri Winner in High-Stakes Week 5 SEC Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS College football analyst Greg McElroy has made his pick for No. 8 Florida at No. 25 Missouri. The ESPN host sees running back Jadan Baugh and the Gators' ground game as the biggest problem for a Tigers team that just lost its conference opener. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy picked Florida to win 31-24 on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. "Florida has a deeper offense," he said, "and Missouri's red zone issues, that's something that's difficult to overcome in this game." Florida jumped from No. 21 to No. 8 in the Top 25 poll after a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss. Missouri slid from No. 19 to No. 25 after it gave up the last 14 points in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. "So, for Missouri, this is got-to-have-it mode, given what's coming up here in the next few weeks," McElroy said. McElroy has liked this Florida team since the summer , when he said the Gators could play spoiler in the 2026 Playoff race. How can Missouri slow Jadan Baugh? Florida Gators running back Jadan Baugh (13) reacts after a play against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baugh, a junior from Atlanta, has 600 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns through four games. He ran for 142 yards and three scores against Ole Miss. That gave him five straight 100-yard games , a streak only Emmitt Smith and Fred Taylor had put together at Florida. That gave him five straight 100-yard games , a streak only Emmitt Smith and Fred Taylor had put together at Florida. McElroy called the Missouri run defense "Missouri's best unit against Florida's best player." The Tigers have stopped 45 runs at or behind the line of scrimmage, which he said ranks in the top six in the country. Quarterback Aaron Philo has completed 72% of his passes for 917 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Still, Florida throws only 26 times per game, which McElroy said ranks 103rd. "If Missouri can somehow hold Jadan Baugh under three yards a carry, then it goes squarely on Philo's shoulders, and we haven't seen it just yet," McElroy said. Florida's secondary faces Missouri passing attack Missouri Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons (13) passes the ball | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons has 11 touchdown passes and no interceptions, according to McElroy, and wide receiver Cayden Lee had 156 receiving yards at Mississippi State. McElroy sees that as the biggest mismatch. He said Florida gives up about 250 passing yards per game and that Ole Miss threw for 298 against the Gators. "So, if Missouri is at, say, 300 passing yards, they have a real chance to potentially win the game," McElroy said. Florida may also get its top receiver back. Vernell Brown III leads the team with 17 catches for 271 yards , and Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said the knee injury Brown suffered against Ole Miss is a mild strain . Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall talks with quarterback Aaron Philo (12) during a timeout against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy picked the Gators by seven. No. 8 Florida visits No. 25 Missouri after beating No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28, and my Florida vs. Missouri predictions still lean toward the Gators being in a tricky road spot. The top pick is Under 57.5, while Missouri's first-half moneyline offers a way to account for the emotional win without fading Florida across 60 minutes. Head over to our latest college football picks for more Week 5 betting analysis. Who will win Florida vs Missouri: Florida -5.5 The Florida Gators just beat top-five Ole Miss 52-28, so a letdown argument is obvious with a road trip to face the Missouri Tigers ahead. But I'm not letting that erase the matchup. I'll play the Gators to -6. Florida ranks 14th in net adjusted EPA per play , while Missouri sits 72nd overall and 107th offensively. The Tigers' defense is the reason this is not a runaway. It ranks 31st overall and third in pass success rate allowed. Florida can attack the softer part of the matchup on the ground, where its rushing offense ranks fifth in EPA per rush against Missouri's 50th-ranked rush defense. There's not a ton here to get you believing in head coach Eli Drinkwitz either. Since 2024, Missouri is 1-9 versus ranked teams, with its only win coming against No. 24 Boston College in 2024. TOP PICK Florida vs Missouri Over/Under pick: Under 57.5 I'm playing the Under down to 57%. If there's any hangover from Florida, this is one of the best ways to capitalize on it. A few late stat-padding touchdowns from the Gators made this number overinflated. The Tigers rank sixth nationally in defensive success rate and third in pass success rate allowed. Florida will score, and I expect the Gators to cover, but they may need to earn points with longer drives instead of relying on constant explosiveness. On the other side, I anticipate the Gators' defense to make Missouri uncomfortable. That unit has allowed just 0.07 EPA per play on early downs. That should help keep Missouri behind schedule, especially given that its offensive success rate sits ranks in the triple digits nationally. Florida vs Missouri combo Missouri's defensive efficiency should keep this from becoming an early track meet, but Florida comes with the stronger profile in the downs that decide close games. The Gators convert 61.9% of third- and fourth-down opportunities , sitting sixth nationally, while Missouri's offense converts 42.9%, ranking 74th. That gives Florida a better chance to sustain the possessions that matter most after halftime, even if Missouri's field position and home environment produce an early lead. A competitive first half followed by Florida's superior talent and coaching taking over is the vision for this combo. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads How fired up are Florida fans over how things are going since Jon Sumrall was hired? The team is now No. 8 in the two major polls after a fun 52-28 win over Ole Miss for the program's first 4-0 start since 2019. Missouri (3-1) lost a 31-24 thriller at Mississippi State last week, but it's good enough to slow down the Gator steamroller. The Tigers won each of their first three games by double-digits, but they'll have to put the offense into high gear to pull this off. Florida vs Missouri: Quick Hits The home side has won the last four meetings since 2019. Mizzou won 33-31 in 2023. The Tigers host Texas A&M next week, and then they're off to Ole Miss. Florida gets South Carolina next week in Gainesville, and then it's on – at Texas, Georgia. Philo has been wonderful so far, hitting 72% of his passes and averaging a monstrous 14.6 yards per completion. Missouri's run defense has been outstanding so far, but it got ripped apart by Mississippi State star Kamario Taylor , who threw for 360 yards and three scores in the Bulldog win. Why Missouri Will Win Missouri has the pass rush to bother Philo. The Florida offensive front is one of the best in the nation in pass protection, but that's partly because defenses have worked so hard to stop Baugh that they haven't been able to go full bore into the backfield. There might have been issues against Mississippi State last week, but the Tigers got to Taylor four times. Mizzou quarterback Austin Simmons hasn't been airtight accurate over the last two weeks, but he threw for close to 300 yards with three scores against MSU, and he has yet to throw a pick. Florida is allowing 248 yards per game. Florida vs Missouri Prediction, Betting Lines This should be a back-and-forth fight. Each defense will do its best to take over and make big things happen, but each side will be flailing with both passing games going off. The difference will be on the ground. Missouri's run defense has been strong so far, but Baugh and the Gators will have the balance to take just enough pressure off Philo to keep scoring. Time, date, TV, prediction for Week 5 Dan Rorabaugh, USA TODAY NETWORK - Florida Wed, September 30, 2026 at 10:05 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's been great to be a Florida Gator in 2026. First-year coach Jon Sumrall has brought one of the nation's most electrifying offenses to Gainesville, and he'll take that show to Missouri this week for another clash between ranked teams. UF is 4-0 (2-0 in SEC) for the first time since 2019 and has already matched its win total from Billy Napier's final season. They picked up their biggest win in years with an exhilarating 52-28 win over then-No. 6 Ole Miss behind 268 combined rushing yards and four touchdowns from Jadan Baugh and Duke Clark . Quarterback Aaron Philo ran one in too, tacking on a TD pass to give him seven on the year. Mizzou (3-1, 0-1) catches Florida 's fifth-ranked offense a week after falling 31-24 to the fourth-ranked offense in Mississippi State. Austin Simmons kept up as best he could with Kamario Taylor , throwing for 295 yards and three touchdowns, with Cayden Lee bringing in 11 catches for 156 yards and two of those scores. Jamal Roberts , starting at running back for the injured Ahmad Hardy , is third in the SEC with 395 rushing yards. Buy Florida vs. Missouri football tickets Here's when the Gators and Tigers square off this week. Florida football schedule: UF's next game What time is Florida vs Mizzou? The Gators and Tigers kick off at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, Missouri . Florida vs Missouri football prediction The Gators passed their first road test of the season two weeks ago at Auburn, a game they led by multiple scores for much of the second half. The two Tigers are tied for seventh in the SEC in allowing 20.8 points per game, but Mizzou is much better defending the run, surrendering just 100.3 yards per game, a hair ahead of Florida for sixth in the conference. They held Kansas , owners of the No. 49 run game in the nation, to just 80 yards on 36 carries, so don't be surprised if Jadan Baugh falls under his lofty averages. The question then becomes whether Aaron Philo can pace the offense, and nothing we've seen so far indicates he can't do it. Both offenses are likely to try to air it out against the other's weaker pass defenses (Missouri is 10th in the SEC in that category, Florida 15th). Eli Drinkwitz's side hasn't beaten a top-10 team in nine tries, though, with two of those coming in Columbia. UF should have enough offense to survive. Prediction: Florida 27, Missouri 21 UF football vs Missouri tickets To see a full list of ticket prices, visit StubHub . Off to their best start since 2019, the 4-0 Gators look to make it five straight against the SEC opponent. Ahead of Week 5's gridiron action, USA TODAY Sports' panel of seven writers submitted their picks for every game played among those ranked in the US LBM Coaches Poll top 25, including this Saturday's showdown inside Memorial Stadium. Only one of the seven respondents — Blake Toppmeyer, who has predicted correctly 61 out of 74 tries this season so far — chose the home team. The other six — John Brice (63-11), Matt Hayes (66-8), Jordan Mendoza (66-8), Paul Myerberg (63-11), Erick Smith (61-13) and Eddie Timanus (64-10) picked the Orange and Blue to prevail. Mizzou leads the all-time series dating back to 1966, 7-6, but the record is knotted up at an even 6-6 since joining the SEC. The Tigers won the previous two meetings in Columbia in 2021 and 2023, but the Gators have prevailed in three of the past five matchups. Florida enters the game ranked eighth in both the Coaches Poll and the AP Top 25 , while Missouri is ranked 25th in both major polls. The faceoff at Faurot Field begins at 3:30 p.m. ET and will be broadcast on ABC. away.headline: UF injuries: No. 8 Gators hopeful WR Vernell Brown III can play at No. 25 Missouri
away.blurb: GAINESVILLE — Gators coach Jon Sumrall is hopeful leading receiver Vernell Brown III will be available during No. 8 Florida's visit Saturday at No. 25 Missouri. Brown injured his right knee while being tackled on a 6-yard run during the second quarter of Florida's 52-28 win against then-No. 4 Ole Miss. He jogged off the field with a slight limp and did not return while wearing a protective sleeve on his leg. The injury is a low-grade strain, Sumrall said, but Brown's timeline to return is uncertain. Meanwhile, receiver Bailey Stockton will be limited during practice this week. away.blurb: As expected, Mizzou (3-1, 0-1 SEC) will again be without star running back Ahmad Hardy, who opened the week on the Wednesday, Sept. 30, report as “out.” The Tigers also listed starting defensive ends Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen as "questionable" for the game against the Gators, which Eli Drinkwitz indicated would be the case during his press conference Tuesday. A questionable designation means neither Smith nor Kitchen have officially been ruled out but will continue to be assessed throughout the week. If Smith can't play, Daeden Hopkins and Jaden Jones are Mizzou's likely starters at defensive end. Smith was helped off of the field during MU’s win over Troy this past Saturday. He attempted to return after being evaluated for a lower-body injury in the second half but only lasted one snap before returning to the sideline. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of MU's Week 4 game against Mississippi State and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. Hardy’s timeline for a return after being shot in the upper leg in May is still uncertain. Florida (4-0, 2-0) listed two wide receivers — Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton — on the report as questionable. Both players have been involved in the Gators' wideout rotation this year, and Brown leads the team in receiving. For the second straight week, Mizzou also ruled out right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. The Tigers added backup linebacker Bobby Washington as "questionable" to face Florida. DE Langden Kitchen (Questionable) LB Bobby Washington (Questionable) WR Vernell Brown III (Questionable) WR Bailey Stockton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. away.headline: Final score, recap from Florida's Week 4 win vs Ole Miss in the Swamp
away.blurb: Florida ran out the clock after the interception and got the required first downs. Kati George spoke to Sumrall again after the game. Gators defense forces quick three-and-out — Florida 45, Ole Miss 28 (Q4 | 8:42) Ole Miss goes three-and-out without gaining a yard, burning just 29 seconds before punting it back to Florida with 8:42 remaining. Florida doesn't give Ole Miss much time to enjoy making it a three-point game. After London Montgomery's 74-yard kickoff return puts the Gators at the Ole Miss 26, Aaron Philo immediately finds Amir Jackson for 23 yards down to the 3. The Gators get an immediate spark on the ensuing kickoff, though, as London Montgomery breaks a 74-yard return to the Ole Miss 26. Florida plays conservatively after getting the ball back with 1:11 remaining. Jadan Baugh runs twice before Aaron Philo finds Dallas Wilson for four yards on third-and-11, bringing out the punt team. Alec Clark flips the field with a 70-yard punt that goes out of bounds at the Ole Miss 2. The Rebels pick up 29 yards on three plays but run out of time. Clark has only had three chances to impress as Florida's punter. This should put him on the map... somewhere. Florida keeps the Rebels out of the end zone from there. DJ Coleman violently breaks up a pass intended for Samari Reed on second down, and Chambliss can't connect with Horatio Fields on third-and-4. Florida starts buried at its own 13 after an ill-advised kickoff return but spends the next 7:15 methodically marching 87 yards on 15 plays. Jadan Baugh gets things moving with gains of seven and two before Aaron Philo converts third-and-1 with his legs. Baugh takes it from there. He gains three yards on a direct snap and punches it in from two yards out on the next play for his second touchdown of the game. The Gators lead by two touchdowns three minutes before the break. The Gators' defense figures it out after that, though. Frazier loses two yards, Jayden Woods drops Caleb Odom for a 5-yard loss and Florida keeps a third-and-17 completion to six yards. Lucas Carneiro connects from 36 yards out, cutting Florida's lead to 10-3 with 10:13 remaining in the half. Penalties wipe out Gators touchdown as drive unravels — Florida 10, Ole Miss 0 (Q2 | 12:34) Baugh takes over from there, gains two yards, then punches it in from four yards out for the touchdown. Jadan Baugh wasted little time getting Florida’s offense moving, ripping off a 12-yard run on the Gators’ first play from scrimmage. Aaron Philo followed with a quick out route to Luke Harpring for another first down, to move Florida into Ole Miss territory. Florida passed its first major test last weekend against Auburn, and while Jon Sumrall and Co. out-duked the Tigers, it was far from a perfect performance — particularly the penalty issue that has once again reared its head. The offense overall still looks potent and the defense, despite a few letdowns, appears to be rounding into form. Jadan Baugh led the way with 142 yards and three touchdowns

home.headline: No. 8 Florida visits No. 25 Missouri, last loss in Columbia serving as Gators' motivation
home.blurb: Florida and Missouri are set to clash in an SEC football matchup on Saturday. Despite their limited history, recent games have sparked a smoldering rivalry between the Gators and Tigers. Florida has lost three of its last four at Missouri's Faurot Field. The Gators, ranked No. 8, are off to a strong start this season, matching last year's win total and defeating then-No. 4 Ole Miss last week. Missouri, ranked No. 25, aims to bounce back after a loss to Mississippi State. Both teams have some injury concerns with Florida wide receiver Vernell Brown III and Missouri edge rushers Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith all questionable. Missouri hopes to have starting edge rushers Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith available as both have been dealing with lower-body injuries. The Gators likewise hope to have their leading receiver, Vernell Brown III, who strained a knee against Ole Miss. He has 17 catches for 271 yards and two touchdowns to go with two punt return TDs. The Tigers remain without their All-American running back, Ahmad Hardy, who was shot as an innocent bystander following a concert in Mississippi in the offseason. Hardy has yet to return to practice, leaving Jamal Roberts in the feature role. picks.headline: Staff predictions for Virginia vs Florida State — a high-end rematch on deck
picks.blurb: Staff predictions for Virginia vs Florida State — a high-end rematch on deck Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB To keep pace and maintain a tie for first place in the ACC, Virginia must conquer Florida State in its first true road game of 2026. An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. This should be a Cavaliers win by multiple scores. Steve DeShazo: Virginia 31, Florida State 27 Saturday brings Virginia's first true road game of 2026. It comes against a proud and talented team that has not played up to its capabilities and may be competing to save Coach Mike Norvell's job in the same way I believe the Cavaliers did for Elliott last year. FSU's offensive skill trio of quarterback Ashton Daniels, receiver Ousman Kromah and receiver Duce Robinson will be a handful for the Cavaliers to contain. Beau Pribula could have a field day passing against the Seminoles, and it may be mandatory to keep Virginia close. The Cavaliers have yet to win a close game or pull out a victory away from home this season. Their only true test came at Charlotte, where the defense struggled and the offensive line showed some vulnerability in a 38-27 loss to West Virginia. Loading recommendations... Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m., and the game will be televised on ESPN2. Of the 21 meetings between FSU and UVA, Saturday marks only the third time (2006, 2010, 2026) that neither team is ranked in the Associated Press Top 25. Florida State (2-2, 0-1 ACC) and the Cavaliers (3-1, 1-0 ACC) will meet for the second straight season and the 21st time overall in UVA's first true road game of the '26 season. FSU and UVA have not met in back-to-back seasons since the 2010 and 2011 seasons, with FSU holding a 15-5 all-time record against UVA, including a 9-1 record at Doak. Virginia's only victory came in 2011 when the Wahoos defeated the then-No. 23 Seminoles, 14-13. UVA will be trying for its third consecutive win and fourth in its last five meetings with the Noles. Saturday will be a rematch of last year's double-overtime loss by then-No. 8 FSU in Charlottesville, which ended with a game-sealing interception in the end zone by the Cavaliers. The victory was UVA's first over a top-10 opponent at home since defeating then-No. 4 Florida State 26-21 in 2005. FSU's 17 Red Zone conversions are the 4th most in the country among the 19 teams that are still perfect inside the 20. Daniels is the only player in FBS in 2026 with multiple rushing and passing touchdowns and a two-point conversion. On the season, the Noles' offense is ranked a not-so-nice 69th in total offense, 76th in the nation in 3rd down conversions with just a 40.8% rate on 20-of-49 attempts, and tied for 63rd in scoring offense with a 32-point average per game. FSU's 126th-ranked total defense is allowing 430 total yards per game, 290 passing yards per game (135th out of 138 FBS teams), and ranked 121st in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 46% of the time on third-down attempts. FSU's boom and bust offense does a nice job of putting points on the board in bunches, but when you have a defense that cannot get off the field (even when playing inferior opponents), it is essential that you consistently sustain success on offense. Noles247.com staff predictions for Florida State's game versus Virginia at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Fla. on Saturday afternoon: Virginia's defense is a solid, though far from outstanding, unit. But in a game where possessions are going to be limited, I question Florida State's ability to slow down the Cavaliers' offense enough for Ashton Daniels and company to keep up with them, given what they've shown over the first month of the season. That starts in the trenches, where Virginia appears to have a significant advantage over the Seminoles' undersized defensive line. Even if Florida State can come out firing as they did early against Alabama , the Cavaliers will stick to what has brought them success this season and wear down the Seminoles' front as the game rolls into the second half – where they could be hurt by play action from Pribula as the second level gets antsy trying to jump into the backfield. The path to victory for Florida State comes from putting Pribula under the pressure he hasn't faced this season, forcing him into a mistake, and capitalizing with points off a turnover. But between Pribula and Daniels, the latter has been more prone to do so, and when the possession battle will be so important, one of those unforced errors could be costly for the Seminoles' chances of coming away with the victory. I think Florida State's offense will find some success, especially from Ousmane Kromah and the rushing attack. But as the game continues, the Seminoles' defense will struggle to get off the field, and Virginia will control things on the ground on its way to a win in Tallahassee. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 20 I find this to be a particularly interesting matchup as both have multiple ways to win. There a lot of "good vs. bad" matchups for both teams in this game. Virginia's ability to run the ball vs. FSU's 1200 thread count soft run defense. Florida State's skill talent on offense vs. a decidedly mediocre Cavalier secondary. Etc. Etc. The position that I will be the deciding factor is quarterback. Both teams will score, and Virginia will 100% limit the overall possessions by holding onto the ball. That means the importance of every possession is magnified. Every explosive you hit carries that much more weight, but every turnover is catastrophic. It all comes down to which team plays a cleaner game and limits unforced errors. I'm taking Virginia. Prediction: Virginia 34, Florida State 27 Florida State can win this game, but I am not convinced they will. My concerns is that Virginia , led by quarterback Beau Pribula , will find consistent success running into the heart of the FSU defensive line, controlling the game, the clock, and exhausting a defense that lacks capable depth and talent. An offense with the oldest offensive line in the country can control this game and should be able to manufacture multiple clock-eating touchdown drives against a Seminole defense that leaves plenty to be desired. They are efficient through the air, though they aren't built to push it down the field aggressively. My reason for optimism when it comes to the Seminoles is that I find Virginia's defense to be susceptible. In the loss to West Virginia , the Cavaliers struggled with a quarterback who ran at them in key moments, though Michael Hawkins Jr. has more wiggle than Ashton Daniels . A couple physical backs for the Mountaineers found success, too, and I think Ousmane Kromah , who should probably see his heaviest workload of the season, can do the same. Also, Virginia will give opportunities on the outside in 1-on-1 coverage and FSU can win there, specifically Duce Robinson who will likely be very motivated after his performance, which included some tough moments, in Charlottesville last season against UVA. Finally, UVA safety Ethan Minter is a player that can be attacked on the seam or vertically with athletic wide receivers. Game can easily swing via turnovers, and that is an area where Virginia is far better than FSU at not committing them on offense and forcing them on defense. I don't have strong feelings either way with one team being an overwhelming favorite. Prediction: Virginia 31, Florida State 28 I've gone back and forth on this game. To be honest both teams are mediocre middle to bottom half of the ACC caliber teams right now. Both quarterbacks leave a lot to be desired. The skill on defense is not up to snuff with years past for either program. That being said, UVA does possess the better offensive line while FSU has the superior skill talent. What does all of that mean? Well it's going to be a battle of styles. Florida States passing attack against UVAs rushing attack. FSU must find explosive wins in the passing game at a more consistent rate while UVA tries to control the ball with a high success rate rushing attack. If Ashton Daniels can be aggressive against the man looks UVA will show him then FSU can win this game. If Ashton Daniels is passive this is going to get ugly in a hurry. I'm going to try a bit of optimism… Prediction: Florida State 34, Virginia 27 Kolby Crawford Everything is telling me to pick Virginia. Bad roster construction up front on both sides, an undersized line that can't hold up against a team built to run right at you, a season already bleeding attendance and goodwill. Which is exactly why I think Norvell comes out with a great plan and jumps on them early at home. Call it surprise, call it vibes, whatever it is, I feel it this week. I still believe this season takes a downturn fast from here, but this is one of the last wins they scrape out before it does. Slang that thing, Ashton. Prediction: Florida State 27, Virginia 23 Virginia had a promising start to the season but that loss to WVU in pretty convincing style is starting to negatively shape my perception of this team. To me the eyes test doesn't bear out against the advanced analytics. F+ has them as a top 25 defense and not a top 25 offense. That doesn't really track with what I see. Their offense is plodding and efficient. They use their mobile QB well, get their 3-4 yards a pop with a well structured IZ scheme, and then work for shots over the top off of play action. Think our offense from last year but without Duce and maybe a more consistent QB. Their defense struggled against WVU. To be honest, they looked good against NCSU but my middle school flag football team could look good against a Dave Doeren offense. Their secondary seems a bit slow and I think if you can spring into the second level you can rip off some chunks. They have a solid front six though which they try to lean on but I think FSU can find some success getting Duce and Kromah outside. This will be a dog fight in my estimation but I gotta give the benefit to the QB I trust more. away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. home.headline: Updated week 5 injury report adds to a growing issue within Florida State's defense
home.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. The updated injury report delivered a few positive bits of news for Florida State, as Ashlynd Barker, Chris Jones, KJ Kirkland, Donny Hiebert, and Xavier Tiller were all upgraded

picks.headline: South Carolina vs Kentucky Predictions: Will the Gamecocks End an Ugly SEC Losing Streak This Weekend?
picks.blurb: South Carolina vs Kentucky Predictions: Will the Gamecocks End an Ugly SEC Losing Streak This Weekend? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM GAMECOCKS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM GAMECOCKS BB This may be one of the most important games of the Shane Beamer era on Saturday. The season is on the verge of running off the tracks and the result of this game could smooth things out for another week or completely derail the entire season. Who comes out on top in a battle between former SEC East foes? South Carolina is in the midst of an eight game losing streak to Power Four opponents, which includes seven losses to SEC teams. During this losing streak Beamer's Gamecocks have fallen to Alabama (twice), LSU, Oklahoma, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, and Ole Miss. Their last win came against Kentucky in a 35-13 route of the Wildcats. However now with Will Stein at the helm, this is not the same Kentucky team of recent years. Wildcats QB Kenny Minchey and this offense have been very efficient and moved the ball well. They got a statement win earlier in the year at College Station and are looking for another. What may help South Carolina in this one is Kentucky's leaky defense . The Wildcats rank 14th in scoring (25 ppg), 12th in rushing (122.25 yards per game), and 13th against the pass (234 yards per game). Rain may be in the forecast for this weekend. This very well could play right into the Gamecocks' hands as they have a much improved rushing attack from last season. Sep 27, 2025; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks students cheer before the game against the Kentucky Wildcats at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect South Carolina Gamecocks on SI Staff Score Predictions South Carolina Gamecocks on SI Staff Score Predictions Alex Joyce: South Carolina 31, Kentucky 20 It appears the rain may hold off, or at least won't be the downpour it was expected to be early in the week . With that said, I believe the Gamecocks are in for a bounce back spot on Saturday. Kentucky's defense will give up plays through the air and on the ground. Kendal Briles should be able to mix up the play calling well and allow LaNorris Sellers to get into a groove. Matt Fuller has topped the 100-yard mark twice in the last three games. I believe he hits that number once again and officially puts a bad losing streak to an end. Joey Walraven: South Carolina 24, Kentucky 21 This game is a must-win for the South Carolina Gamecocks. A loss here could potentially be cement another losing season for the Gamecocks and be the final touches on Shane Beamer's exit . With those implications, I expect LaNorris Sellers to have his best game of the season and lead the Gamecocks to a hard fought victory. Sellers will cetainly need to play well, but the difference in this game will be on the ground. The Gamecocks boast the best rushing attack in the SEC as well as allowing the fourth fewest average yards of on the ground in the conference. Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. South Carolina game glance, opening odds, and early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CBS parts ways with analyst Tony Romo TRENDING Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Kentucky vs. South Carolina game glance, opening odds, and early prediction chrisbeasmore Wed, September 30, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 24 Kentucky football did not look its best in the first half against South Alabama, but the Wildcats took a 24-21 lead into halftime thanks to a two-minute stretch that featured a rushing touchdown, an interception, and a field goal just before the break. The second half was a complete 180, as Kentucky shut out South Alabama and pulled away for a 45-21 victory, and the victory improved Kentucky to 3-1 overall and 1-1 in SEC play. Now, the Wildcats will take on a struggling South Carolina team on the road. The last time Kentucky was on the road, the Wildcats defeated then-No. 9 Texas A&M, 31-21, in College Station. The victory showed how strong Kentucky's defense can be while also giving quarterback Kenny Minchey an opportunity to show what he can become as he continues to develop under first-year head coach Will Stein. South Carolina Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2) The Shane Beamer era is facing increased pressure in Columbia, as South Carolina enters the matchup on a seven-game SEC losing streak. The Gamecocks' last SEC victory came against Kentucky on Sept. 27, 2025, when South Carolina defeated the Wildcats 35-13. South Carolina opened the 2026 season with a dominant 57-0 victory over Kent State, but the Gamecocks have since struggled against SEC competition. South Carolina lost 41-34 at home to Mississippi State before falling to Alabama 49-18 on the road this past weekend. The loss to Alabama dropped the Gamecocks to 0-2 in SEC play. Now, Kentucky comes to Columbia, making this a potentially significant game for Beamer and the Gamecocks. Kentucky is also looking to snap a four-game losing streak against South Carolina. Doing so under Stein would give the Wildcats another significant road victory during his first season. South Carolina will also be without star EDGE Dylan Stewart, who has been suspended indefinitely by Beamer and more than likely will not play against Kentucky. Stewart's suspension came after the Gamecocks' loss to Alabama, during which he threw a punch at Alabama tight end Josh Ford and had a heated interaction with South Carolina's coaching staff. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains one of South Carolina's biggest offensive weapons. The dual-threat quarterback opened the season with 270 passing yards and three touchdowns in the Gamecocks' win over Kent State. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is another player Kentucky will need to account for. Harbor returned to South Carolina for the 2026 season alongside Sellers and remains one of the team's most important receiving threats. Junior running back Matt Fuller is also a name to watch in the South Carolina backfield after showing his ability as both a runner and receiver. ESPN gives Kentucky a 42.1% chance of winning. My Early Prediction: Kentucky has already proven it can win on the road after defeating then-No. 9 Texas A&M. Why can't the Wildcats do it again? South Carolina is on a seven-game SEC losing streak and will be without Stewart, while Kentucky enters the matchup ranked No. 24 in the AP Top 25 and coming off a dominant second half against South Alabama. Kentucky also has plenty of motivation to snap its four-game losing streak against the Gamecocks. Why not us? Final Score: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 27.

Mark Stoops was fired in December after 13 seasons and Will Stein is now leading the program. He was hired out of Oregon where he was the offensive coordinator. South Carolina 's last SEC win was more than a year ago vs Kentucky for a seven-game conference losing streak. Kickoff is 4:15 p.m. on Oct. 3 (SEC Network) in Williams-Brice Stadium . The Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2 SEC) lost to No. 8 Alabama 49-18 on Sept. 26. The Wildcats (3-1, 1-1) beat South Alabama 45-21 in Week 4. Here's the Greenville News' prediction for how the game will go. The Wildcats are 3-1 and have a big-time road upset as they took down the Texas A&M Aggies, who were ranked #9 at the time. While the hype and excitement are there, the Wildcats have a big-time game on Saturday on the road against the South Carolina Gamecocks. picks.headline: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CBS parts ways with analyst Tony Romo TRENDING Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats have to go on their second road trip of the season as the will face off against South Carolina at 4:15 P.M. ET on Saturday. We have previewed both South Carolina offense and defense, as well as laying out Kentucky's path to victory in this game. This is a massive game for both teams; Kentucky is trying to snap a four game losing streak against the Gamecocks and South Carolina is a desperate trying to turnaround their season. In this article, I will give my final thoughts on the game and a prediction. Kentucky has to win early downs in this game, and they have consistently done that all season on both sides of the football. Kentucky's offense has stayed ahead of schedule consistently and haven't needed to rely on converting third downs, which has been a weak spot for this offense. Kentucky's offensive line has improved every week and they have to dominate the line of scrimmage in this game. They have been phenomenal in run blocking as they lead the country in yards before contact per rush attempt, and they should keep Kenny Minchey clean as South Carolina is without their game-wrecking edge defender Dylan Stewart. Defensively, Kentucky has performed similarly as the offense. They are struggling on third downs, but they have been exceptional on early downs. If they can slow down this South Carolina run game and keep their offense off schedule, it should bode well for the Wildcats defense. Kentucky will probably have a similar defensive gameplan that they had against Texas A&M, contain LaNorris Sellers on the ground and force him to beat you with his arm. Sellers has struggled this season, he has turned the ball over four times. The turnover margin has been the downfall of Kentucky in this series as of late, as the Wildcats have 14 total turnovers in the last five matchups against the Gamecocks. That could flip on Saturday, Kentucky is +3 in the turnover margin on the season, whereas South Carolina is -4 in the turnover margin. Kentucky has done a great job at taking care of the football and creating turnovers on defense. South Carolina has their backs against the wall, head coach Shane Beamer is on a scorching hot seat. They have struggled against SEC opponents and the talk surrounding their program has been extremely loud this week. Combine that with your best player serving a suspension, it will be a lot to overcome for the Gamecocks. Who gets off to a hot start could be the determining factor in this football game. Speaking of hot starts, there are multiple reasons it could play a factor in this game. South Carolina needs to create that early momentum to keep the crowd involved. If Kentucky gets off to a hot start and the Gamecocks struggle offensively, you could see the boo birds come out in Columbia from this fan base. It is worth noting, Kentucky ranks third in the SEC this season in time trailing this season, as the Wildcats have only spent a total of over 26 minutes trailing through the first month of play. Kentucky has been good at getting off to quick starts this season, and I could see that continue on Saturday. Kentucky has a unique offensive scheme that will force a struggling South Carolina defense to communicate. Over the last five meetings, the Wildcats have averaged just 13 points per game, which is the main reason they have been 1-4 over that stretch. I believe Kentucky gets the offense going and South Carolina fails to overcome all the noise surrounding the team this week. Prediction: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 24 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction

(Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Jordan Kaye Fri, October 2, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads South Carolina returns to Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday, desperately needing a victory over No. 24 Kentucky (3-1, 1-1 SEC). The Gamecocks have not won an SEC game in over a calendar year, a drought that dates back to the last time USC faced the Wildcats (Sept. 27, 2025). The good news for USC: South Carolina has won its last four matchups against Kentucky and leads the all-time series 22-13-1. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on SEC Network. The Gamecocks are 3.5-point favorites. Those are some facts. Here are some thoughts. 1. We're talking about practice? Shane Beamer is infatuated with talking about practice. South Carolina has won two of its last 13 games against Power 4 competition, has lost seven straight SEC games and was blown out by Alabama on Saturday. Things are dire. But rather than eat some humble pie, Beamer on Tuesday seemed to take pleasure in inciting the fan base. "People get tired of hearing about the wrong thing, well guess what?" We had a hell of a practice today," Beamer said, nodding his head over and over. "We had a hell of a practice. So, if you get tired of hearing that, I'm sorry. You're gonna keep hearing it." This is not to discount the importance of practice, but why would anyone take Beamer's comments at face value given what we've seen over the last two years? This is not new. In his postgame news conference after a blowout loss to Oklahoma last year, Beamer touted the Gamecocks' great week of practice , adding: "Our guys were focused, had a hell of a walkthrough (Friday) at the stadium." Who was that for? Who heard that and took solace in USC's performance, or gained some newfound optimism? A number of fans on social media this week took it upon themselves to name the Gamecocks the national champions of practice, with one user joking, "Let's get that banner up in Willie B (ASAP)." Perhaps Beamer knows his job status might be decided over the next few weeks. What's unclear is why he continues to needle Gamecock fans with his comments about practice. 2. LaNorris Sellers might not trust his receivers Against Alabama, there were three throws in the first 35 minutes where QB LaNorris Sellers completely missed an open receiver on very short throws (0-9 yards). These are throws he probably completes 99 out of 100 times in practice , the kind of misfires that would only make sense if his hands were covered in grease. So why is he missing them in the game? "I wish I could put my finger on it exactly," offensive coordinator Kendal Briles said Wednesday. The most plausible explanation: He has little faith in his receivers. He's thinking too much, trying to be perfect because he knows anything short of perfection might lead to another drop. Of course, one can imagine the toll of that could lead to uncharacteristically wild throws. Now, this is not an excuse. Sellers is a senior. He has to be able to make those throws without thinking, fire a ball to an open receiver and live with the results. Great quarterbacks should be able to overcome surrounding faults. But Sellers' pass catchers have let him down. Consider: Out of every FBS quarterback in America this season, per Pro Football Focus (PFF), only Stanford's Davis Warren (17) has had more passes dropped than Sellers (14). Even more: The Gamecocks' receivers have only come down with 4 of 13 contested throws (50-50 balls). 3. The busts are baffling South Carolina has given up multiple touchdowns in the last few weeks because of coverage busts, which is hard to wrap one's head around. Defensive coordinator Clayton White and DBs coach Torrian Gray have been at USC for six years. The defense hasn't changed. The verbiage hasn't changed. And most of South Carolina's secondary are very experienced players who started or played for the Gamecocks last year. So why now are there so many blunders? Part of it has to do with the lack of pass rush. Both Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor and Alabama's Keelon Russell had solid protection and were able to stay in the pocket for four, five seconds before firing a pass. The longer a play develops, the better chance a bust occurs. But, too often, guys are just in the wrong spot. "Some of it is on me on some untimely calls," White said. "Obviously, the other part has been execution. Just always want to take ownership wherever things are." 4. Gamecocks need to rely on Matt Fuller As if this South Carolina team hasn't endured enough bizarre weather this season , the forecast calls for moderate rain in Columbia while the Gamecocks and Wildcats are playing. Get ready for a handoff fest at Williams-Brice. And if that's the case, advantage South Carolina. The Gamecocks are averaging more rushing yards per game (262) than any team in the SEC and managed to rack up a combined 362 yards on the ground in their two conference games. Kentucky, meanwhile, has barely cracked 200 total rushing yards in its pair of conference matchups. So far, running back Matthew Fuller has proven to be South Carolina's top offensive weapon — he's tallied nearly 500 yards from scrimmage this season — and it seems likely that he'll carry the ball 20-plus times (he had 19 carries against Alabama) and be the focal point of USC's offense. 5. Vegas is usually right Last week, ahead of Florida's matchup against Ole Miss, Gators head coach Jon Sumrall was asked about his team being 3.5-point favorites. He seemed perplexed. "Who has us favored against these guys?" Sumrall asked reporters. "There's a lot of good drugs out there, huh?" It was odd that the Rebels were underdogs just a week after proving themselves with an impressive win over LSU. As is often the case, the Las Vegas oddsmakers were onto something. Florida won easily. Which brings us to Saturday. There is no logical reason South Carolina should be favored against any ranked football team right now, especially by 3.5 points. It is a suspicious line, as if the folks in Las Vegas know or see something the rest of us don't. But it feels fishy in a way that should make every Gamecock fan optimistic. Prediction: South Carolina 24, Kentucky 20

Trending VIP Three potential coaching targets for South Carolina if Shane Beamer is fired One final look at the matchup between South Carolina and Kentucky. A beleaguered South Carolina team returns to the field on Saturday afternoon but will return home to play in front of another sold out crowd at Williams-Brice Stadium against Kentucky. The Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2) just haven't been real close in their opening two games of Southeastern Conference play and need a win in a bad way over a Wildcats (3-1, 1-1) team that already has one ranked road win. Sixth-year head coach Shane Beamer needs a win in the worst way as his seat couldn't get much hotter. A national report earlier this week from On3 said, to paraphrase, a loss to the Wildcats may bring an end to Beamer's tenure. But both the Gamecocks and Beamer have an opportunity to on Saturday afternoon to win their fifth straight game over the Wildcats, which played a lackluster first half a week ago against South Alabama before dominating the second half for what ended up being a comfortable win. While we usually have a VIP member pick with us, messages to multiple members who volunteered went unanswered. Perhaps that's the mood of the fanbase as a whole, or perhaps we just picked the wrong folks. Either way, it'll just be the Gamecock247 staff this week. If accessing this story from Plano's Roost message board, click on the link just below to continue reading. South Carolina vs. Kentucky – Hale McGranahan (Photo: Ryan Bethea, 247Sports) For this exercise, we're going to tune out all the noise and forget all of the implications this game has, in terms of long-term outlook for the program. South Carolina's first two SEC opponents of the season were much greater challenges than what Kentucky will bring into Williams-Brice on Saturday. This is the type of matchup Clayton White and Torrian Gray should be able to handle just fine, same with their players. The Wildcats don't have a quarterback with first-round potential. They don't have multiple wide receivers who are a threat to score anytime they're on the field. The running backs are pretty good, but they're not super explosive rushers, though the top two did pop some big runs last week. South Carolina's defense has a much better chance to look like the one we've seen more often than not over the last five years. Offensively, the Gamecocks should be able to move the ball on the ground. Finishing drives – something they've struggled with this season – will be a critical element to the whole deal though. Can't keep settling for field goals, even though this game probably won't be a shootout. Assuming the forecast holds, it's going to be a rainy afternoon at Williams-Brice, which will help make this game feel like a bit of a slog. That 53.5 total seems awfully steep. South Carolina 28 – Kentucky 20 South Carolina vs. Kentucky – John Whittle (Photo: Jordan Prather, USA TODAY Sports) Let's start by saying that South Carolina should not lose to Kentucky in football. I forget which one of our illustrious message board posters coined the phrase "Blue Vandy," but it's brilliant. It's the way that the Gamecocks should view the Wildcats in football … and really any sport besides basketball. But that doesn't mean that South Carolina is going to win this game. Captain Obvious here, but this game could really go one of two ways. The Gamecocks could rally behind their embattled head coach and deliver their best performance of the year, despite being without the top defensive player on the team, who's suspended. Or, they could tie their bindle to the end of a stick and walk out on the rest of the season with another loss. The Wildcats got pummeled at home against Alabama , but turned around and knocked off Texas A&M on the road. Last week's win over South Alabama was a slog in the first half, but the Wildcats pitched a 21-0 shutout in the second half to end in a lopsided win. First-year head coach Will Stein seems to have brought some real energy into the program, which is not something that South Carolina has right now. The Gamecocks are struggling to find answers to key questions in all phases of the game. The offense is moving the ball, but can't score. And the defense can't stop anyone, giving up a crazy number of explosive plays. There's been almost no analysis from myself or anyone else about the actual game in these picks, so I'll just say that if the Gamecocks win this game, it'll be in large part because of the run game. And if it's because of the run game, it's time that the Gamecocks officially enter the chat of being one of the best in the country in that aspect of the game. Is it really going to be another messy day weather-wise at Williams-Brice Stadium? And is it going to be another messy performance? Hopefully it's neither, but it's really hard to pick the Gamecocks right now. Kentucky 33 – South Carolina 31 South Carolina vs. Kentucky – Alex Jones (Photo: Ryan Bethea, 247Sports) Not that this needs to be said again, but this is a massive game for Shane Beamer and South Carolina . Kentucky doesn't have the weapons on the perimeter that the last two opponents had but do have what it takes in Will Stein's offense to have success through the air. That's important every game, but with the noise around the program, the pressure would absolutely increase on the Gamecocks if the Wildcats get out to an early lead. I think the Gamecocks are able to run the ball and win by eight. Defensively, losing Dylan Stewart is so unfortunate, especially against a Kentucky team that's physical. I think South Carolina comes out with a lot more urgency at Williams-Brice. Even if it rains. picks.headline: How No. 24 Kentucky football & South Carolina match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 19 of 25 passes for 177 yards with one touchdown throw in UK’s 45-21 victory over South Alabama last week. For the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey, a fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, is completing 68.3% of his throws for 876 yards. The Notre Dame transfer has thrown eight TD tosses vs. one interception. • South Carolina’s LaNorris Sellers is 2-0 as a starter vs. Kentucky. In those two games, Sellers has completed a combined 21 of 28 passes for 319 yards with two TD throws vs. one interception and has also run for 70 net yards on 22 carries. On the season, Sellers, a 6-3, 238-pound fourth-year player, has completed 62.1% of his throws for 833 yards with six TDs but has thrown four picks. A Florence, South Carolina, product, Sellers has run for a net 244 yards and a touchdown. Advantage : South Carolina Running backs • Kentucky is coming off the first game in school history in which the Wildcats had three running backs rush for 100 yards or more in the win over South Alabama. CJ Baxter 6-1, 230-pound, fourth-year player who transferred from Texas, led the way with 149 rushing yards and a touchdown vs. USA. Junior Jason Patterson went for 137 yards and three touchdowns against the Jaguars, while Oklahoma transfer Jovantae Barnes ran for 100 yards and a score. On the season, Patterson is sixth in the SEC in rushing (326 yards) and Baxter is eighth (313). A 5-10, 204-pound third-year player, Patterson is leading the SEC in yards per carry at 8.15 yards a rush. • South Carolina’s Matt Fuller leads the Gamecocks in rushing with 384 yards (fourth in the SEC) and in receptions with 13 (for 113 yards and a touchdown). In South Carolina’s 35-13 win over Kentucky last season, Fuller, a 5-11, 221-pound third-year player from Jesup, Georgia, ran for 48 yards on 19 carries. Jabree Coleman has run for 147 yards this season but is averaging 8.6 yards a carry and has scored three touchdowns. Isaiah Augustave has run for 107 yards in 2026 but is averaging 8.2 yards a carry and has scored two TDs. Advantage : Kentucky Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby has 13 receptions and leads the Wildcats in receiving yards with 226. LSU transfer Nic Anderson caught two passes for 21 yards vs. South Alabama. Southern Utah transfer Shane Carr caught his first UK touchdown last week against USA and finished with two catches for 22 yards. • South Carolina’s Nyck Harbor ranked No. 1 on The Athletic’s 2026 college football “Freak’s List.” A 6-5, 239-pound product of Washington, D.C., Harbor has an 82.5-inch wingspan and has run a 10.1-second 100-yard dash. On the football field, Harbor has 11 catches for 169 yards and a touchdown in 2026. In last season’s win over UK, Harbor caught one pass for 10 yards. Mazeo Bennett Jr . has 10 catches for 169 yards and a TD this season. In South Carolina’s 31-6 victory over Kentucky at Kroger Field in 2024, Bennett caught three passes for 63 yards and a touchdown. • Kentucky’s Henry Boyer tied for the team lead with three catches in the win over South Alabama. A 6-6, 270-pound senior from Chicago, Boyer has made seven catches for 110 yards and two TDs on the season. Ex-Covington Catholic star Willie Rodriguez leads the Wildcats in receptions (17) and is second in receiving yards (137). Second-year player Mikkel Skinner has seven catches for 91 yards and a TD. • South Carolina’s Brady Hunt has made nine catches for 81 yards and has a long reception of 20 yards. Hunt caught one pass for 15 yards vs. UK last season. Maurice Brown II has five receptions for 38 yards and a touchdown. Brown caught one pass for 10 yards against Kentucky in 2025. Offensive line • Through four games, Kentucky center Coleton Price is drawing rave reviews from Will Stein. Of the 6-3, 308-pound Baylor transfer, Stein said “He’s one of the best players on our team. I think he’s one of the best players in the country, specifically at his position. And he’s a leader. He’s a smooth athlete. He’s powerful. So I would say he’s playing very well.” • A highly-regarded transfer from North Carolina State, South Carolina left tackle Jacarrius Peak missed the first two games of 2026 as he recuperated from an offseason knee injury. However, Peak has now returned to claim a starting position. True freshman right tackle Darius Gray was the No. 2 interior offensive line prospect in the high school class of 2026 and has started all four games for far for the Gamecocks. Gray started at left tackle the first three weeks but flipped to right tackle for last week’s 49-18 loss at Alabama. Advantage : Even Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace leads the Wildcats in sacks (2.5) and tackles for loss (three). The 6-4, 291-pound Cincinnati product is also tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (three) and has both an interception and a pass breakup. • South Carolina star end Dylan Stewart was suspended by Gamecocks coach Shane Beamer after Stewart drew a penalty for punching an Alabama player during last week’s blowout loss to the Crimson Tide. In two previous games vs. Kentucky, Stewart had a combined seven tackles, 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. Right defensive tackle Tomiwa Durojaiye has made 10 tackles and recorded two sacks. The 6-4, 291-pound Durojaiye started his college career at UK in 2022 and has subsequently played for West Virginia, Florida State, Illinois and now South Carolina. • After Kentucky weakside linebacker Bo Barnes was ejected vs. South Alabama for targeting, fifth-year player Alex Afari logged his most significant playing time of 2026 and led the Wildcats in tackles with nine. Because of uncertainty about his eligibility, Afari did not have a full preseason in the new UK defensive system. “I think he’s becoming more instinctual in this defense. (It) takes some time to get used to, just because it’s a different scheme than he was used to,” said Kentucky coach Will Stein. “When you know what to do, you can play more aggressive and make more plays.” • South Carolina MLB Fred “JayR” Johnson , a 6-3, 241-pound third-year player, led the Gamecocks with eight tackles in the loss at Alabama. WLB Justin Okoronkwo is South Carolina’s leading tackler on the season with 26. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior free safety Jordan Castell is the second-leading tackler in the SEC with 36 stops. A transfer from Florida, Castell also has two interceptions and two passes defended. Strong safety Ty Bryant is 11th in the SEC in tackles with 30. • South Carolina nickelback Quay’sheed Scott was the starter at the same position last season for Kentucky. A 5-11, 208-pound product of Marion, South Carolina, Scott has made five tackles and successfully defended three passes in 2026. Strong safety Peyton Williams is third on the Gamecocks with 16 tackles and has an interception. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 4 of 5 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 52 yards. Punter Thomas O’Hara , a transfer from Murray State, is averaging 40.7 yards a kick on 11 punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Punt returner Brock Coffman lost a fumble that set up a South Alabama touchdown last week. • South Carolina punt returner Vicari Swain ran two punts back for touchdowns (45 and 58 yards) in the Gamecocks’ 45-9 victory over Towson in Week 2. In his career, Swain has five punt-return TDs, good for the South Carolina career record. Place-kicker Malik Orsan is 5 of 6 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 52 yards. Punter Mason Love is averaging 44.3 yards on 10 kicks, and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. away.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Eagles open conference play at Coastal Carolina with a 1-3 record, plus key injury updates following Saturday’s loss to No. 25 Houston. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4. Georgia Southern and Coastal Carolina kick off Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. from Brooks Stadium in Conway, South Carolina. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the biggest ACC games of the season takes place Saturday night as No. 4 Miami heads to Death Valley to take on Clemson . Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, Clemson (3-1) matters again after being left for dead following the 51-10 loss to LSU to start the season. The late rally against North Carolina and a better-than-it'll-get-credit-for win over Cal got the Tigers to 2-0 in the ACC, and if they can somehow pull this off, the expectations go through the roof. Miami (4-0) won its first four games without much of an issue. Before dogging the schedule without any marquee wins, respect the long road trip win over Stanford to start the season. And as it turns out, beating Wake Forest by 13 was excellent. Miami vs Clemson: Quick Hits Miami gets two straight home games after this, with a week off before hosting Florida State and Pitt. Clemson gets a week off, and then a breather against Charleston Southern before picking things back up with Virginia Tech . The Tigers don't play a road game until October 31st against Florida State. Miami won the last meeting in 2023, but won the previous four – including the 2017 ACC Championship – going back to 2010. How To Watch Miami vs Clemson Date: Saturday, October 3, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Memorial Stadium, Clemson, SC – Week 5 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 5 Why Miami Will Win How has Clemson turned this around over the last two weeks? The rushing attack took over late against North Carolina to pull off the win, and it dominated Cal with 48 carries for 257 yards. Miami's run defense isn't allowing a thing. No, the talent on the defensive front isn't as good as last year's team when it comes to pass rushers, but this season's line has been a wall, giving up fewer than two yards per carry with no touchdowns allowed. Sep 26, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) leads his teammates onto the field before the game against the Central Michigan Chippewas at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Why Clemson Will Win The Tiger defense is starting to step up. It was fantastic against the North Carolina and Cal passing games, and the two takeaways in each game turned out to be a big deal. This is when the Tiger passing game has to open it up a little bit. It hasn't done anything crazy with freshman Tait Reynolds easing his way into the season, but he's got the ability to make things happen – he was great against North Carolina. Wake Forest hung around with the Hurricanes with 312 passing yards, and Reynolds will have to come up with close to that. Miami vs Clemson Prediction, Betting Lines Clemson and Dabo Swinney are 16.5-point underdogs at home? Yeah, that seems crazy, but it's not like the Tigers haven't been hit hard at home in the recent past, losing by 13 to Syracuse early last year and by 12 to Louisville in 2024, but it still doesn't seem quite right. Miami will struggle to get going, and then QB Darian Mensah will find his groove. Clemson's defense isn't great on third downs, and the offense is even worse – it's only converting on 27% of its chances. The Canes are seventh in the nation in third down conversions, and Mensah will keep connecting on them in the second half.
