(Patrick Breen/The Republic) 1 / 29 Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney How much of this game will have to be decided by Reynolds, who is a freshman? This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Clemson vs. Miami scouting report Where Clemson has an advantage: Miami hasn't faced a secondary as good as Clemson's. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Miami also looks better on the other side. Marquise Lightfoot is tied for fourth in the ACC with four sacks, while Damon Wilson II and Armondo Blount can win one-on-one. Miami generated pressure on 60.8% of Wake Forest's dropbacks in its last ACC game, and Reynolds is 20 of 46 for 175 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions when he's under pressure or blitzed. The Hurricanes might be better than LSU. They have arguably the nation's best quarterback, one of the nation's most electric wide receivers and a dominant defense. Miami is better in too many areas. picks.headline: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire?
picks.blurb: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CBS parts ways with analyst Tony Romo TRENDING Browns outlast Steelers Duren, Pistons reach deal Joey Porter Jr. trade grades Yankees oust Red Sox Fantasy Football Trade Tips Sam Navarro-Imagn Images; Ken Ruinard-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 1, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Canes and Tigers will have the eyes of the nation on them on Saturday night in a big game for two programs going in different directions. The Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers square off on Saturday night in Death Valley in a game with significant ACC title implications, with the game being shown in primetime on ABC. The Canes have surged to a 4-0 start, with only a slight flutter in the second half at Wake Forest after leading 31-7 being their only show of mortality thus far. Meanwhile, Clemson has improved to 3-1 after a season-opening 51-10 loss at LSU. Lifeless performances against Georgia Southern and in the first half against UNC have turned into a come from behind win over the Tar Heels and an impressive 24-10 win at Cal last weekend. Can the Tigers ride that modest improvement into an upset win on Saturday night? Our college football writers weighed in with their game predictions. Miami 38, Clemson 28 I think the writing is on the wall for Clemson and Dabo Swinney. The program is a shell of itself, esepcially from a talent acquisition standpoint. Things are the exact opposite for the Hurricanes, as they were less than 70 yards away from a national championship. Even so, I expect Clemson to show out for this game almost as a last ditch effort to save their season. It won't be enough, as the Hurricanes prove to be too explosive for the Tigers. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 30, Clemson 10 This game had the potential to be one of the better matchups in the ACC this season if Clemson held up their end of the bargain, but it looks like Dabo and the boys have only fallen further down the list in terms of program competence. The quarterback position is a mess, and a lot of the notable draft prospects heading into the season simply haven't played up to the offseason hype. On the other hand, you have a Miami team with not only one of the sport's most explosive weapons in Malachi Toney, but also one of the most efficient passers in college football in Darian Mensah. I know Clemson is at home, but this has a chance to be a route for the Hurricanes. Give me Miami, big. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 34, Clemson 21 This game is much closer than the final score suggests, with Clemson hanging around for a large portion of the afternoon. One of the biggest storylines will be how the Tigers handle Malachi Toney. It'll be interesting to see if Clemson allows CB Ashton Hampton to follow Toney around the field and essentially shadow him, considering Hampton is the most talented defensive back Miami has faced to this point. If Clemson can limit Toney and force Miami to win elsewhere, the Tigers have a chance to make this uncomfortable. Ultimately, though, Miami's overall talent takes over as the game progresses. The Hurricanes make enough explosive plays on offense to create separation, while Clemson capitalizes on a couple of coverage busts from the Miami secondary for some big plays of its own. Miami's depth and playmakers prove to be the difference in the second half, allowing the Hurricanes to pull away and finish with a 34-21 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Miami 30, Clemson 13 This feels like a game that could be closer than many pundits are giving it credit for, and perhaps those in Las Vegas as well. The 17-point line feels out of place for what Clemson has been over the last decade, but Dabo Swinney's Tigers have looked anything but the part of contenders the last few years. Clemson's secondary is talented, led by Ashton Hampton, who could play himself into first round consideration in April's NFL Draft. I could see the Tigers giving Miami's offense problems and preventing some of the chunk plays that Miami has ripped off all year with the exception of a quarter and a half against Wake Forest. But Clemson freshman QB Tait Reynolds is going to have a rough experience against a Miami team that's starting to get a tad healthier on the defensive side of the ball. DL Ahmad Moten, Sr. and Armondo Blount are off the injury report and appear set to be available on Saturday, along with CB Damari Brown. Starting CB Xavier Lucas could even possibly be in play, but even if not, Ethan O'Connor has been one of the better CBs in the ACC this year and can handle things very capably. Miami slowly puts this one away in the second half with Mark Fletcher, Jr., who is also off the injury report, pounding away in the fourth quarter on a tired defense. The No. 4 Miami Hurricanes will take on the most successful ACC program of the last 15 years with a road game at Clemson on Saturday night. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. EST and the game will be televised on ABC. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, UM is a 15.5 point favorite. The weather forecast for the game calls for 75 degrees and a 30 percent chance of rain at kickoff. Miami (4-0, 2-0) won the last match-up against Clemson, a 28-20 double overtime victory at Hard Rock Stadium. The Tigers won the previous four match-ups against the Hurricanes. UM's last win at Clemson was a 30-21 victory in 2010. Clemson (3-1, 2-0) was throttled by LSU, 51-10, in the season opener and the Tigers have responded with three straight wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, and California. The Hurricanes enter the game with one of the most explosive offenses in the country, averaging 51.8 points per game, which ranks third nationally. Miami is averaging 7.3 yards per play, which ranks fourth nationally. UM is converting 55.6 percent of their opportunities on third down, which ranks seventh, and the red-zone touchdown rate is 80.9 percent, ranking 15th best in the country. UM's defense is allowing nine points per game (4th nationally) and 4.3 yards per play allowed (14th nationally). The Hurricanes have allowed opponents to convert 29.1 percent of opponent's third down opportunities (24th nationally) while the red-zone touchdown rate checks in at 40 percent (No. 10 nationally). The Tigers enter this game averaging 21 points per game, which ranks 120th in the country, and 4.7 yards per play, which ranks 106th nationally. On third down, Clemson is converting just 27.3 percent of their opportunities, which ranks 133rd in the country. The Tigers have earned a 36.36 percent red-zone touchdown rate, which ranks 135th nationally. Clemson's defense is allowing 22 points per game (63rd nationally) and 5.1 yards per play (51st nationally). CU's third down defense is allowing opponents to convert on 39 percent of their opportunities and the Tigers have allowed a red-zone touchdown rate of 60 percent, which ranks 72nd in the country. Saturday night's game is an opportunity for Miami to further confirm they are the dominant program of this current ACC landscape while Clemson will fight to make a statement that their reign isn't quite over yet. How do the teams match-up on paper going into Saturday night's game. Read on for our match-up breakdown and predictions for the game. (Photo: Getty) The Hurricanes rank first in the country in team passing efficiency while averaging 361 yards per game through the air and averaging 10.9 yards per attempt while completing 86.3 percent of their attempts as a team. Quarterback Darian Mensah is completing an eye-popping 88.7 percent of his attempts with 1,211 yards and 14 touchdowns against zero interceptions. Mensah has not committed a turnover-worthy-play through the first four games, according to PFF. Mensah has earned a 93.9 passing grade from PFF through four games, which is the highest grade in the country. Mensah has been elite at the deep ball this year, completing 10-of-14 passes that have travelled at least 20 yards downfield for 356 yards and five touchdowns. Slot receiver Malachi Toney is Mensah's top target in the passing attack, totaling 564 yards and six touchdowns on 34 receptions. Toney is second in the country in yards after catch with 243 YAC on the year. According to PFF, UM's pass blocking grades out as the 58th best in the country. UM is allowing 0.75 sacks per game. Miami's offensive linemen have not allowed a sack this season, according to PFF. Left tackle Samson Okunlola has earned a 79.9 pass blocking grade this season. Clemson's passing efficiency defense ranks 19th in the country as the Tigers have allowed 214 yards per game through the air. The Tigers are in year two of the Tom Allen era at defensive coordinator and in 2026, Clemson has played the fourth most man coverage in the country as the defense looked to simplify things on the back end after a poor showing in 2025. The strength of the Clemson pass defense is the pass rushing ability of defensive end Will Heldt, who has 17 pressures and four sacks on the season, and cornerback Ashton Hampton, who is one of the best cover corners in the country. Both players are expected to be selected in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. Penn State transfer cornerback Elliot Washington has picked off three passes this season. Hampton has recorded seven pass break-ups already. According to PFF, the Clemson pass rushing grade ranks 81st in the country while the coverage grade ranks 26th. Edge: Miami. This is a real strength vs. strength match-up, but the explosiveness of UM's passing attack gives them the edge. (Photo: Getty) Miami is averaging 227 rushing yards per game, which ranks 20th in the country, while averaging 6.32 yards per attempt, which ranks tenth nationally. Mark Fletcher leads the way with 260 yards on the ground and three rushing touchdowns while averaging 6.4 yards per attempt. Fletcher was held out of the week four contest against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and is expected to be a full go at Clemson. Fletcher is averaging 5.44 yards per carry after contact while forcing 15 missed tackles. UM lost their RB2 for the season with CharMar Brown sustaining a serious leg injury at Wake Forest and true freshman Javian Mallory has now seen his role elevated. Mallory has run for 226 yards and three touchdowns while averaging nine yards per carry. According to PFF, Mallory is averaging an impressive 6.44 yards per carry after contact. Girard Pringle is a change of pace running back who can be a receiving threat out of the backfield (4 receptions for 43 yards) and Jordan Lyle has returned from an early season suspension and is looking to find his rhythm and knock off the rust. The right side of the offensive line has graded out well in run blocking with RT Matthew McCoy (72.7 grade), RG Max Buchanan (76.3 grade), and C Ryan Rodriguez (75.0 grade) all grading out with a 70.0+ PFF run blocking grade. The Clemson run defense is allowing 157 yards per game on the ground, which ranks 97th in the country and the Tigers average 4.3 tackles for loss per game, which ranks 103rd. Safety Corey Myrick, who is a transfer from Southern Miss, leads the team with 35 tackles while middle linebacker Sammy Brown has totaled 33 tackles, two tackles for loss, and one sack. According to PFF, Clemson's run defense grade ranks 97th in the country while the tackling grade checks in at 123rd in the country. Edge: Miami. The Clemson run defense has been poor, especially considering that the Tigers primarily play man coverage, which allows the front seven to focus on stopping the run. (Photo: Cory Fravel, 247Sports) The Clemson passing operation has been a disaster this season. The Tigers rank 133rd in the country in passing efficiency while averaging 155 yards per game through the air while throwing only two touchdowns this year. True freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while completing 64.3 percent of his passes. According to PFF, Reynolds has earned a 52.1 passing grade. Reynolds has completed 2-of-15 deep shots for 47 yards with one touchdowns and two interceptions. Despite Clemson's passing attack being putrid, the Tigers do feature a trio of receivers with NFL Draft potential in T.J. Moore, Bryant Wesco, and Tyler Brown. Moore and Wesco are talented outside receivers while Brown operates from the slot. The talented wide receiver trio is being stunted by the play of the quarterback, however. The Tigers have allowed 2.75 sacks per game this season, which ranks 116th in the country. According to PFF, the Clemson pass blocking grades out as the 69th best in the country. UM's passing efficiency defense ranks 17th best in the country with the Hurricanes allowing 185 yards per game through the air. Miami is averaging 2.50 sacks per game, which ranks 37th nationally, and the Hurricanes have picked off two passes. Miami's trio of defensive ends—Armondo Blount, Marquise Lightfoot, and Damon Wilson—have combined to generate 31 quarterback pressures and 6.5 sacks. Nickel Omar Thornton has been a threat as a blitzer as well, generating eight quarterback pressures. UM lost their starting corners, OJ Frederique and Xavier Lucas, in the season opener against Stanford. Ethan O'Connor has elevated into a starter role and performed at a high level while earning an 89.1 coverage grade from PFF while picking off one pass. Bryce Fitzgerald has moved from safety to cornerback and has allowed just four receptions for 31 yards on nine targets. PFF grades the Hurricanes with the third best passing grade in the country while the coverage grade ranks 57th nationally. Edge: Miami. The Hurricanes have a big edge in this phase. away.headline: Who would Clemson turn to if Tait Reynolds gets hurt against Miami?
away.blurb: Christopher Vizzina has returned to practice and is available after suffering a left elbow injury against Georgia Southern, but he has not completely recovered. News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Who would Clemson turn to if Tait Reynolds gets hurt against Miami? Drew Landon Clemson Wire Sept. 30, 2026, 7:01 p.m. CT The Tigers have already dealt with one quarterback injury this season, so who would Clemson turn to if freshman starter Tait Reynolds gets hurt? According to head coach Dabo Swinney, fifth-year quarterback and former walk-on Trent Pearman would currently be the first player off the bench. “He can throw, but he’s still not 100% on his left arm,” Swinney said. Swinney explained that Vizzina’s primary limitation is his range of motion as he works toward returning to full strength. Although Vizzina could play if needed, Pearman would currently receive the first opportunity behind Reynolds. Vizzina opened the season as Clemson ’s starter before injuring his non-throwing elbow against Georgia Southern. Reynolds replaced him and has since started Clemson’s victories over North Carolina and California. Reynolds is the main guy for now but Trent Pearman is waiting behind him, and who knows, after that maybe Chris Denson could be next in line after that, and we could perhaps see him throwing again in the quarterback position. away.headline: Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury
away.blurb: MIAMI, Fla. – After missing last Saturday's 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium, the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes are set for the return of running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. (both seniors) against Clemson , but it should be taken with caution. The backfield supporting cast suffered a difficult loss of redshirt junior CharMar "Marty" Brown, who is out for the rest of the season with a severe right knee injury, which was sustained against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. home.headline: Who would Clemson turn to if Tait Reynolds gets hurt against Miami?
home.blurb: Christopher Vizzina has returned to practice and is available after suffering a left elbow injury against Georgia Southern, but he has not completely recovered. News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Who would Clemson turn to if Tait Reynolds gets hurt against Miami? Drew Landon Clemson Wire Sept. 30, 2026, 7:01 p.m. CT The Tigers have already dealt with one quarterback injury this season, so who would Clemson turn to if freshman starter Tait Reynolds gets hurt? According to head coach Dabo Swinney, fifth-year quarterback and former walk-on Trent Pearman would currently be the first player off the bench. “He can throw, but he’s still not 100% on his left arm,” Swinney said. Swinney explained that Vizzina’s primary limitation is his range of motion as he works toward returning to full strength. Although Vizzina could play if needed, Pearman would currently receive the first opportunity behind Reynolds. Vizzina opened the season as Clemson ’s starter before injuring his non-throwing elbow against Georgia Southern. Reynolds replaced him and has since started Clemson’s victories over North Carolina and California. Reynolds is the main guy for now but Trent Pearman is waiting behind him, and who knows, after that maybe Chris Denson could be next in line after that, and we could perhaps see him throwing again in the quarterback position. home.headline: Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan
home.blurb: Clemson quarterback Christopher Vizzina (right) injured his left elbow against Georgia Southern, but coach Dabo Swinney (left) said Vizzina will still be available vs. North Carolina. Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina is available, coach Dabo Swinney said, but not 100 percent recovered from a small fracture in his left elbow. What’s the Tigers’ plan if they need a backup to play vs. Miami? Clemson listed Vizzina as a game-time decision in the final availability report before Clemson’s Sept. 19 win over North Carolina. He was left off the final report entirely before the Sept. 25 win at Cal. He was listed as Clemson’s backup quarterback on the depth chart vs. Miami, per team release. Top Story Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan By Jackson Castellano jcastellano@postandcourier.com Jackson Castellano Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said Vizzina is throwing and practicing after sustaining a small left elbow fracture Sept. 12 against Georgia Southern. However, Swinney said that Trent Pearman would be Clemson’s second option at quarterback vs. Miami if necessary. “He's still not 100 percent on his left arm, so if he plays, he plays with a brace on it to protect it,” Swinney said. “But it's really more just the range of motion for him, kind of getting that back fully. But it's gotten a little better each day.” Swinney said Vizzina could play in an emergency. He wasn’t listed in the initial ACC availability report Sept. 30. The senior has 14 completions for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions this season. He was in the running for Clemson’s QB1 job with freshman Tait Reynolds during preseason camp, but Vizzina was ultimately named the starter in Week 1. Vizzina played three drives in the 22-7 win over Georgia Southern before Reynolds took over. The pair had previously split reps in a 51-10 loss to LSU. Reynolds was named the starter moving forward after the Georgia Southern game, but Swinney said the change had nothing to do with Vizzina’s health. In two career starts and four total games, Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Pearman, a fifth-year senior , joined Clemson as a walk-on in 2022. He has 10 passing attempts in his career, completing four for 43 yards. The D.W. Daniel graduate has played 33 career snaps. Reynolds will start for Clemson (3-1, 2-0 ACC) in its Oct. 3 matchup with No. 4 Miami (4-0, 2-0). Reach Jackson Castellano at jcastellano@po
